Every finding this guide has already settled, and everything disclosed for completeness: **2,087 values** across **93 groups**. Nothing on this page is asking for anything. What is still open is on [what needs an answer](open-items.html).

This page exists so that any claim the guide makes about the chapter can be checked against the thing that was observed, without reading the pipeline. It is long by design and is meant to be searched rather than read.

### Answered by committee <span class="ri-count">&mdash; 1 question</span>

Questions this guide put to a committee, and what came back. Each keeps the number it was asked under and the text of the original ask, so that a reference to it made before the answer still lands in the right place.

<a name="gq-does-reordering-a-code-system"> </a>

#### 1. Does reordering a code system's concepts count as a change?

<div class="ri-answered">
<p><b>Answered by TSMG</b> &mdash; Terminology Infrastructure WG meeting, HL7 Plenary, Rockville, 2026-09-21.</p>
<p><b>The ruling:</b> Reordering a code system&#x27;s concepts is not a change, and does not increment the version.</p>
<p><b>What it changed here:</b> None. The comparison already treated concept order as presentation, so no artifact moved and no version number changed. What the ruling settles is the standing of the rule rather than its result: the 32 tables that carry exactly THO&#x27;s codes in a different order keep THO&#x27;s version because the policy owner says they should, and not because this project read the policy that way.</p>
</div>

**What we do:** no. Concepts are compared as a set keyed by code. A code
system whose codes are identical to THO's but listed in a different order is
treated as unchanged and keeps THO's version.

**Why:** order is not information in a flat code system. A `CodeSystem` with
`hierarchyMeaning` of `is-a` and no nesting says nothing by putting `M` before
`F`, and nobody reading the resource learns anything from the sequence.

**How much rides on it:** **32 tables** have exactly THO's codes in a
different order. If order is a change, those 32 all increment, and they
increment again every time the chapter is re-laid-out.

**This is now the only rule behind the version numbers that rests on a
judgement rather than a fact.** Every other increment in this build follows
from a difference the policy names outright.

**If the answer is no:** nothing changes. **If the answer is yes:** it is one
line in the comparison, and 32 more artifacts increment.

#### Concept domains &mdash; Definition differs from tho <span class="ri-count">&mdash; 4 items</span>

<div class="ri-blurb">Chapter 2C and THO describe the same domain differently. THO's wording was kept; decide whether Chapter 2C's should win instead.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key"><code>ContainerForm</code></div>
  0967
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">These are two unrelated definitions rather than two versions of one, so nothing is highlighted.</p>The domain of possible values describing shape or type of the container, e.g.:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Tube/vial<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Jar<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Bag<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Block<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Slide</div>
  <div class="ri-who">THO: <div class="cell">Describes the nature (or type) of the container.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>**Examples:**<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br> *<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Carton<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br> *<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Bottle<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br> *<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Vial<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>**DesignNote:**The material of the container should be separately specified (e.g. the &quot;cardboard&quot; part of cardboard carton or the &quot;glass&quot; part of glass vial should be described elsewhere).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>**OpenIssue:**This usage of material form is used in Common Product Model,but it is at variance of what has been done in Specimen where the same information is captured in the Entity.code values. These differences need further study.</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key"><code>EmploymentStatus</code></div>
  0066
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">These are two unrelated definitions rather than two versions of one, so nothing is highlighted.</p>The domain of possible values for the guarantor&#x27;s employment status.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">THO: <div class="cell">A code used to define the employment status of the insured individual identified in UB-92 FL 58. UB-92 Form locator 64:Employment Status Code of the Insured. Can be used with Employee\_Employer\_statusCode in HL7. Values include Employed Full Time, Employed Part Time, Not Employed, Retired, On Active Military Duty</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key"><code>ObservationMethod</code></div>
  0626
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">These are two unrelated definitions rather than two versions of one, so nothing is highlighted.</p>The domain of possible values specifying the type of Observation Method.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">THO: <div class="cell">A code that provides additional detail about the means or technique used to ascertain the observation.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>*Examples:* Blood pressure measurement method: arterial puncture vs. sphygmomanometer (Riva-Rocci), sitting vs. supine position, etc.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>*Constraints:* In all observations the method is already partially specified by the Act.code. In this case, the methodCode NEED NOT be used at all. The methodCode MAY still be used to identify this method more clearly in addition to what is implied from the Act.code. However, an information consumer system or process SHOULD NOT depend on this methodCode information for method detail that is implied by the Act.code.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If the methodCode is used to express method detail that is also implied by the Act.code, the methodCode MUST NOT be in conflict with the implied method of the Act.code.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>*Discussion:* In all observations the method is already partially specified by simply knowing the kind of observation (observation definition, Act.code) and this implicit information about the method does not need to be specified in Observation.methodCode. Particularly, most LOINC codes are defined for specific methods as long as the method makes a practical difference in interpretation. For example, the difference between susceptibility studies using the &quot;minimal inhibitory concentration&quot; (MIC) or the &quot;agar diffusion method&quot; (Kirby-Baur) are specifically assigned to different LOINC codes. The methodCode therefore is only an additional qualifier to specify what may not be known already from the Act.code.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Also, some variances in methods may be tied to the particular device used. The methodCode should not be used to identify the specific device or test-kit material used in the observation. Such information about devices or test-kits should be associated with the observation as &quot;device&quot; participations.</div></div>
</div>

#### For V2 Management / TSMG &mdash; Answered <span class="ri-count">&mdash; 9 items</span>

<div class="ri-blurb">Register items a committee has ruled on. The original finding and ask are kept alongside the ruling, so that the record shows what was asked as well as what came back.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0010</div>
  <p><b>Table 0010 <i>Physician ID</i> carries no terminology and is withdrawn</b></p><p>Table 0010 is one of three sections in Chapter 2C that declare no concept domain, no code system, no value set and no codes. It is a <code>User</code> table whose description ends &ldquo;No suggested values&rdquo; &mdash; a site-defined identifier that was arguably never a code table. The omission is an outlier rather than house style: of the 149 tables whose description says &ldquo;No suggested values&rdquo;, <b>147 carry a concept domain block</b>. The two that do not are 0010 and 0188. Neither THO nor the UTG repository has a CodeSystem or a ValueSet for it, so nothing was ever minted and nothing needs withdrawing from THO. <b>What it does have is bindings.</b> Fields across several segments &mdash; PV1, IN3, SCD and others &mdash; still name table 0010 in the source of truth, and those bindings point at a table that is about to stop existing.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Answered. Kept because the binding removal is work this project has to do, and the ruling is the authority for doing it.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>V2 Management</b> &mdash; V2 Management call, 2026-10-09.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> Table 10 goes away, and any terminology bindings to table 10 will be removed as v2+ is prepared.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> Nothing changes in the vocabulary IG: this guide already writes no artifact for 0010 and routes it <code>nothing-to-write</code>, so there is nothing to suppress and no artifact to withdraw. <b>The work the ruling creates is in the v2+ IG, not here</b> &mdash; removing the bindings that name table 0010 in <code>input/sourceOfTruth/segment/</code> and the segment intros that document them. That is the structural workstream's to do, and it is recorded here because this register is where the ruling arrived. The companion finding for <b>0188</b>, the only other table of this shape, is <b>not</b> answered by this ruling and stays open as <code>esc-tables-that-should-be-domains</code>.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0188</div>
  <p><b>Table 0188 <i>Operator ID</i> carries no terminology and is withdrawn</b></p><p>The companion of <code>esc-0010-withdrawn</code>, and ruled on the same way. 0188 is one of three sections in Chapter 2C that declare no concept domain, no code system, no value set and no codes. It is a <code>User</code> table whose description ends &ldquo;No suggested values&rdquo; &mdash; a site-defined identifier that was arguably never a code table. The omission is an outlier rather than house style: of the 149 tables whose description says &ldquo;No suggested values&rdquo;, <b>147 carry a concept domain block</b>. The two that do not are 0010 and 0188. Neither THO nor the UTG repository has a CodeSystem or a ValueSet for it, so nothing was ever minted and nothing needs withdrawing from THO. <b>As with 0010, what it does have is bindings</b> that name the table in the source of truth and will point at a table that no longer exists.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Answered. Kept because the binding removal is work this project has to do, and the ruling is the authority for doing it.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>V2 Management</b> &mdash; V2 Management call, 2026-10-14.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> Same situation as table 0010: the table goes away, and terminology bindings to it are removed as v2+ is prepared.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> Nothing changes in the vocabulary IG. This guide already writes no artifact for 0188 and routes it <code>nothing-to-write</code>, so there is nothing to suppress and no artifact to withdraw. <b>The work is in the v2+ IG</b>, removing the bindings that name table 0188, and belongs to the structural workstream exactly as 0010's does. <code>esc-tables-that-should-be-domains</code> now covers only 9999, which was never a table and is not answered by either ruling.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0567, 0568</div>
  <p><b>Chapter 2C deprecates tables 0567 and 0568 &mdash; does anything in THO get deprecated with them?</b></p><p>Both table descriptions say so outright: <i>&ldquo;Note this table has been deprecated and is replacaced by table 0929&rdquo;</i> for Weight Units, and the same sentence naming 0930 for Volume Units. (The misspelling is the chapter's.) But the deprecation was recorded in prose only, and nothing downstream reflects it. <b>The value sets were not deprecated.</b> THO publishes <code>ValueSet/v2-0567</code> and <code>ValueSet/v2-0568</code> as live resources alongside <code>v2-0929</code> and <code>v2-0930</code>, none of them carrying a deprecation marker, and this project reproduces all four. So a consumer reading THO cannot tell that two of the four are superseded. <b>The chapter contradicts itself on identity.</b> Table 0567 prints its own value set URI as <code>http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v2-0929</code> and 0568 prints <code>&hellip;/v2-0930</code> &mdash; the replacement's canonical, not its own. Under the rule that a canonical URL is an identifier and THO's existing one wins, this project publishes them at <code>v2-0567</code> and <code>v2-0568</code>, which is why no collision occurred. Had the chapter's printed URI been honoured, two pairs of resources would have claimed the same canonical. <b>Separately, the contents do not match the description.</b> 0568's concept domain is &ldquo;the domain of possible values of units of measure that are used to specify volume&rdquo; and its code system is UCUM, but it enumerates three codes; 0567 enumerates four. These are a small subset of the UCUM units for the quantity, so the CLD and the description promise a great deal more than the value set delivers.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Two questions, and the first is the one that needs a group rather than an individual. <b>(1)</b> Chapter 2C deprecated these tables; does a concomitant deprecation need to be reflected in THO &mdash; marking <code>ValueSet/v2-0567</code> and <code>v2-0568</code> deprecated or retired &mdash; or does the chapter's prose deprecation stop at the chapter? This project currently publishes both as live, which is fidelity to THO and arguably not fidelity to the chapter. <b>(2)</b> Is the enumerated subset intended, or should these value sets be an intensional reference to the UCUM units for the quantity? Note that whichever way (2) goes, it applies equally to the replacements 0929 and 0930.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>V2 Management</b> &mdash; V2 Management call, 2026-09-23.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> Tables 0567 and 0568 should never have been created. Their value sets will be retired, but not by this IG and not as part of this load: a separate Jira ticket will be raised against THO to retire <code>ValueSet/v2-0567</code> and <code>ValueSet/v2-0568</code>. This IG is to do nothing with them.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> This guide stops publishing both value sets. It had been publishing them at 4.0.0 against THO's 3.0.0 &mdash; an increment earned only by adding display text to codes THO leaves bare &mdash; so the guide was minting a new version of two artifacts it has now been told to leave alone. Suppression is recorded in <code>write_utg_xml.py</code>'s <code>RULED_SUPPRESSIONS</code> and the two tables are reported as <code>suppressed-by-ruling</code>, so the guide says why they are absent rather than being silently short of two artifacts. <b>Question (2) of the ask is not answered and survives this ruling:</b> whether the enumerated subset is intended, or whether these should be an intensional reference to the UCUM units for the quantity. It applies to the live replacements 0929 and 0930, which this guide does publish &mdash; carrying byte-identical code lists to the two tables being retired. It is now asked against those two tables as its own item.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0005, 0567, 0568, 0929, 0930</div>
  <p><b>Deprecating a V2 value set in THO has no established representation, and would be a first</b></p><p>The item above asks whether THO should deprecate the two tables Chapter 2C deprecates. This one is about what that would actually require, because the mechanism is not sitting there ready to be used. <b>There is no CodeSystem to mark.</b> None of the four tables in this family &mdash; 0567 and 0568 and their replacements 0929 and 0930 &mdash; has a CodeSystem in THO or here. All four are value sets enumerating a handful of codes from UCUM, which belongs to somebody else. So <code>ValueSet.status</code> is the only status the artifact has, and FHIR's <code>PublicationStatus</code> offers exactly <code>draft</code>, <code>active</code>, <code>retired</code> and <code>unknown</code>. There is no <code>deprecated</code> in it. <code>retired</code> is available but says something stronger and different: the codes in these value sets are valid UCUM units and are still sent. <b>THO's one artifact-level mechanism has never carried this value.</b> The <code>structuredefinition-standards-status</code> extension appears <b>53 times</b> in the snapshot, on 53 different resources, and every single one of them says <code>trial-use</code>. The <code>deprecated</code> code is defined in <code>CodeSystem/standards-status</code> and is perfectly bindable &mdash; it has simply never been used. So the representation that matches the facts here &mdash; <code>standards-status = deprecated</code> with <code>.status</code> left <code>active</code>, because the codes remain valid &mdash; would be the <b>first use of that code in THO's history</b>. That is a precedent, not a data entry. <b>A successor pointer needs a third element again.</b> R5's ValueSet has no <code>replacedBy</code>. The available shape is <code>relatedArtifact</code> with <code>type = successor</code> aimed at <code>v2-0929</code> and <code>v2-0930</code>, and nothing in the snapshot does that for a v2 value set either. <b>Worth recording: the replacement-canonical confusion is inside THO as well, not only in the chapter.</b> The item above notes that Chapter 2C prints the replacement's canonical as 0567's own URI. THO's <code>CodeSystem/v2-tables</code> does the same thing: entry <code>0567</code> carries <code>v2-vs-uri</code> = <code>http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v2-0929</code> and entry <code>0568</code> carries <code>&hellip;/v2-0930</code>, while both also carry the comment &ldquo;replaced by 0929&rdquo; and &ldquo;replaced by 0930&rdquo;. The index knows the tables were replaced and has overwritten their identity with their replacements' instead of recording the relationship. The value set OIDs are shared outright: <code>2.16.840.1.113883.21.452</code> is the identifier on both <code>ValueSet/v2-0567</code> and <code>ValueSet/v2-0929</code>, and <code>&hellip;21.453</code> on both <code>v2-0568</code> and <code>v2-0930</code> &mdash; two more instances of one OID on two artifacts.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Settle the representation before the instance, because either answer sets a precedent. If a deprecated V2 table's value set is to be marked in THO, confirm the shape: <code>standards-status = deprecated</code> on the artifact, <code>ValueSet.status</code> left <code>active</code>, and <code>relatedArtifact</code> <code>type = successor</code> pointing at the replacement. If that is not the intended use of the extension, say what is &mdash; because at present there is no way to say &ldquo;deprecated&rdquo; about a THO value set that anything has ever done. <b>A sibling question of the same shape, which THO has already half-answered against itself.</b> <code>CodeSystem/v2-0005</code> is <code>retired</code> and all five of its concepts carry <code>status: deprecated</code>, while <code>ValueSet/v2-0005</code> is <code>active</code>. Does retiring a v2 code system oblige any action on the value set published at the matching canonical? Note that the two are not the same content: the value set does not compose from the retired code system at all &mdash; its single include is six CDC race codes from <code>urn:oid:2.16.840.1.113883.6.238</code> &mdash; so a second question comes with it, whether a value set named <code>v2-0005</code> that contains none of table 0005's codes is correctly named. Both are about THO's own records rather than about anything this guide writes, which is why they are parked here rather than acted on.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>V2 Management</b> &mdash; V2 Management call, 2026-09-23.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> Both halves are settled, and neither lands on this IG. The 0567/0568 retirement goes to THO as a separate Jira ticket, so no deprecation needs representing here. For table 0005, the value set stays and the code system is correctly retired already; this IG will not link the value set and should not inform any change to it.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> Nothing is published differently on account of 0005 &mdash; the guide was already neither altering nor linking <code>ValueSet/v2-0005</code>. What changes is that this is now a decision rather than an omission. The representation question the item was really about &mdash; whether marking a THO value set deprecated would need <code>standards-status = deprecated</code>, the first use of that code in THO's history, plus a <code>relatedArtifact</code> successor pointer &mdash; is <b>not answered, only avoided</b>. The Jira ticket that retires 0567 and 0568 will meet it again, because <code>retired</code> still says something stronger than the facts: the UCUM codes in those value sets remain valid and are still sent. <b>Recorded here because the next person to need it should not have to rediscover it.</b> So are the two findings about THO's own records that no ruling touched: <code>CodeSystem/v2-tables</code> carries the replacements' canonicals as 0567's and 0568's own <code>v2-vs-uri</code>, and the value set OIDs <code>&hellip;21.452</code> and <code>&hellip;21.453</code> each sit on two artifacts at once.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0411</div>
  <p><b>Table 0411 <i>Supplemental Service Information Values</i> is concept domain only</b></p><p>Split from <code>esc-0460-user-defined-mint</code>, which asks what a user-defined table should produce across three tables; 0411 has been answered and 0460 and 0093 have not. 0411 was one of only <b>two</b> tables in the whole chapter for which this guide minted a new CodeSystem canonical &mdash; every other code-bearing table either reuses a THO canonical or draws on another authority's code system. THO has no CodeSystem and no ValueSet for it, so both resources were first publications. The table is <code>Type: User</code> and lists two codes, <code>NDBS</code> and <code>CG</code>. It also carries the defect recorded under <code>esc-retain-known-errors</code>: the chapter prints a canonical for a code system resource that does not exist.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Answered. Kept because the two codes the chapter publishes stop appearing anywhere as a result, which a reader of the chapter may come looking for.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>V2 Management</b> &mdash; V2 Management call, 2026-10-14.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> Table 0411 should be concept domain only, so no code system and no value set.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> Both <code>CodeSystem/v2-0411</code> and <code>ValueSet/v2-0411</code> are withheld. This removes one of the two minted canonicals, and with it the defect that the chapter prints a canonical for a resource that does not exist &mdash; it now does not exist here either, deliberately. <b>The chapter's two codes, <code>NDBS</code> and <code>CG</code>, are no longer published as concepts anywhere.</b> That is what the ruling asks for and it is worth stating plainly, because it is content the chapter prints and this guide now does not. The concept domain is unaffected. <b>0460 and 0093 are not answered by this ruling</b> and stay open on <code>esc-0460-user-defined-mint</code>. The original finding asked for the three to be treated alike; this ruling moves 0411 to the same outcome as 0093, which leaves <b>0460 as the only minted canonical in the corpus</b> and makes it more of an outlier than it was, not less.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0350, 0351</div>
  <p><b>Tables 0350 and 0351 are not concept domain only, and their value sets compose over a code system nobody publishes</b></p><p>Split from <code>esc-tho-dangling-value-sets</code>, which covers four tables; these two have been ruled on and 0456 and 0895 have not. <b>The chapter and THO disagree about what these tables are.</b> Chapter 2C flags both <code>Concept Domain Only: yes</code> and prints no code system block, no value set block and no codes. THO's own <code>CodeSystem/v2-tables</code> types both <code>Externally defined</code> and records a code system OID, a value set OID and a content-logical-definition flag for each &mdash; none of which a concept-domain-only table carries. The chapter contradicts itself in the same breath: its table descriptions name the National Uniform Billing Committee and print the code system OIDs <code>2.16.840.1.113883.6.301.7</code> and <code>&hellip;.301.8</code>. <b>THO publishes both value sets, and both are unexpandable.</b> <code>ValueSet/v2-0350</code> and <code>v2-0351</code> are active resources composing over <code>CodeSystem/v2-0350</code> and <code>v2-0351</code>, <b>neither of which THO publishes</b>. Its <code>NamingSystem/v2-0350</code> and <code>NamingSystem/v2-0351</code> map the two NUBC OIDs to those same absent canonicals, so the index asserts the NUBC codes live at a THO URL that serves nothing. <b>There is no NUBC URI to point at instead.</b> THO carries twelve <code>AHA_NUBC_*</code> naming systems &mdash; revenue codes, condition codes, type of bill &mdash; each resolving to a <code>https://www.nubc.org/CodeSystem/&hellip;</code> URI. <b>Occurrence codes and occurrence spans are not among them.</b> The two tables sit on the same OID arc as <code>AHA_NUBC_ValueCodesAndAmounts</code> (<code>&hellip;.301.6</code>), which does resolve, so the registration looks like an omission rather than a decision. The chapter's note that the UB-04 manual is available by subscription is the likely reason no code system was ever minted.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Answered as to classification; <b>the code system is still unresolved and needs TSMG.</b> Either mint <code>CodeSystem/v2-0350</code> and <code>v2-0351</code> so the existing pointers resolve, or register NUBC URIs for occurrence codes and spans as the other ten NUBC systems have and repoint the naming systems and value sets at them. Until one of those happens both value sets are published and cannot expand.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>V2 Management</b> &mdash; V2 Management call, 2026-10-14.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> 0350 and 0351 are <b>not</b> concept domain only. The value sets exist in THO, which makes them v2 content and therefore fair game for revision in this IG, and the fix is to the content logical definitions in the value sets. This corrects the error in Chapter 2C that declares the tables concept domain only.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> Both tables are reclassified <code>value-set-only</code> and this guide now publishes <code>ValueSet/v2-0350</code> and <code>ValueSet/v2-0351</code> where it previously wrote nothing. They carry THO's identity, description and version unchanged, so neither increments. Recorded in <code>write_utg_xml.py</code>'s <code>RULED_RECLASSIFICATIONS</code> &mdash; a third mechanism beside the tentative overrides and the suppressions, because a reclassification adds output and so has to say what to publish and over what. <b>The CLD is reproduced, not repaired, and that is the part the ruling could not reach.</b> The fix asked for is to point the compose at the appropriate external code system &mdash; but there is no such code system to point at. THO registers no NUBC URI for occurrence codes or spans, and the only canonical either value set has ever named is the absent <code>CodeSystem/v2-NNNN</code>. So this guide composes over the same unresolvable canonical THO does: the value sets exist and are correctly classified, and they still cannot expand. The writer reports this on every run rather than letting it pass, and the remaining half is a TSMG question. <b>0456 and 0895 are not answered by this ruling</b> and stay open on <code>esc-tho-dangling-value-sets</code>. 0456 is the same shape &mdash; an NUBC table whose THO value set dangles &mdash; and the reasoning here would likely apply, but it was not named.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0133</div>
  <p><b>Table 0133 says three incompatible things about itself, and THO publishes nine codes for it</b></p><p>Table 0133 <i>Procedure practitioner identifier code type</i> carries three statements that cannot all hold. <b>One:</b> its concept domain block sets <code>Concept Domain Only: yes</code>, and it publishes no code system, no value set and no codes &mdash; so this project writes nothing for it, which is the correct reading of that flag. <b>Two:</b> its own table metadata describes it as a code set: &ldquo;HL7-defined table of concepts which specify the different types of practitioners associated with this procedure. <i>This set of codes is known to be incomplete.</i>&rdquo; A table that is concept-domain-only has no set of codes to be incomplete. <b>Three:</b> the same description says the table is obsolete &mdash; &ldquo;as of v2.6, this table and the field(s) it was used in was replaced by table 443 used in the ROL segment&rdquo; &mdash; yet its <code>Type</code> is <code>undefined</code> rather than anything marking it withdrawn, and it is still published in 2.9.1. <b>Meanwhile THO publishes <code>CodeSystem/v2-0133</code> with nine codes, <code>content: complete</code> and <code>status: active</code>,</b> plus a matching value set. So the chapter says there are no codes, says the codes are incomplete, and says the table was superseded in v2.6, while THO says there are nine active ones. <b>To be clear about what is not anomalous here, so this does not read as a fourth contradiction:</b> a CodeSystem holding the concepts plus a ValueSet whose compose is a single bare include of it is THO's <i>standard</i> pair shape for a v2 table that owns its codes, and this guide generates the same pair for 399 tables. The pair is not the problem. The problem is that THO has anything at all for a table the chapter flags concept domain only and says 0443 replaced in v2.6, and that both resources are <code>active</code> with <code>content: complete</code>. This is why 0133 shows as <i>In THO, not here</i> on the table index: the divergence is real and is not ours to resolve.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Decide what 0133 is. If it was genuinely replaced by table 0443 in v2.6, it should be marked withdrawn in the chapter and its THO code system and value set retired or deprecated, rather than left active. If it is still live, the <code>Concept Domain Only</code> flag contradicts both its own description and THO's nine codes, and one of the three has to give. Either way the description should stop asserting an incomplete code set for a table that publishes none.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>V2 Management</b> &mdash; V2 Management call, 2026-10-14.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> Manipulate the markdown description so it jumps out that this is a discontinued code system as of v2.6 that was replaced.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> The table description now carries a bolded statement ahead of the chapter's own sentence &mdash; <i>&ldquo;This table was discontinued as of v2.6 and replaced by table 0443, used in the ROL segment.&rdquo;</i> &mdash; as markdown, which the publisher renders as bold. It is recorded in <code>vocabulary_text_policy.py</code> under a new <code>EMPHASIS_ADDED</code> table rather than among the corrections, because adding emphasis on a committee's instruction is a different act from repairing a typo and the change log should not conflate them. The chapter's original sentence is kept after the added one, so nothing published is removed and the two can be compared. <b>What the ruling does not change:</b> the table is still <code>Concept Domain Only: yes</code>, so this guide publishes no code system and no value set for it, and THO still publishes nine active concepts at <code>CodeSystem/v2-0133</code> with <code>content: complete</code>. The contradiction between the two bodies is unresolved &mdash; the description now warns a reader about it. Whether THO's pair should be retired is a TSMG question that has not been put to them.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0078</div>
  <p><b>Table 0078 <i>Interpretation Codes</i> duplicates an existing THO value set under a new URL</b></p><p>Split from <code>esc-oid-conflicts</code>, which asked about three OIDs; this third of it has been answered and the other two are still open. Chapter 2C prints the canonical <code>http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v2-0078</code> and the value set OID <code>2.16.840.1.113883.1.11.78</code>. THO publishes nothing at that canonical, so writing it would be a first publication rather than a disagreement &mdash; but the OID is not free. THO's <code>ValueSet/v3-ObservationInterpretation</code> already carries it, on a value set whose content logical definition is <i>byte-identical</i> to the one this guide would write: a single bare include of <code>CodeSystem/v3-ObservationInterpretation</code>, no filter, no enumerated concepts. It is the only ValueSet in the snapshot with either that OID or that compose. Publishing <code>v2-0078</code> would therefore put <b>one OID on two artifacts</b> &mdash; the policy breach <code>esc-oid-conflicts</code> records for 0719.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Answered. Kept because the ledger note the ruling calls for is work this project has to do.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>V2 Management</b> &mdash; V2 Management call, 2026-10-14.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> The value set already exists, just at a different URL: <code>ValueSet-v3-ObservationInterpretation</code>. That value set is allowed to serve and no new one is created. The situation is noted in the ledger. This keeps fidelity to Chapter 2C in as much as the guide is simply not adding something, rather than doing something different.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> <code>ValueSet/v2-0078</code> is no longer written. It had been a first publication at 1.0.0 carrying the chapter's OID, so dropping it removes the second artifact that the OID collision was about &mdash; resolving that third of <code>esc-oid-conflicts</code> without having to choose between two identifiers. The register's option <b>(c)</b> for this table, which the identical compose was said to support. <b>0001 and 0719 are not answered by this ruling</b> and stay open on <code>esc-oid-conflicts</code>: those are genuine conflicts between two existing artifacts, where this one was avoidable by not creating the second.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">32 tables</div>
  <p><b>Does reordering a code system's concepts count as a change for versioning?</b></p><p>This project compares its concepts against THO's as a set keyed by code, so a code system whose codes are identical to THO's but listed in a different order is treated as unchanged and keeps THO's version. The reasoning is that order is not information in a flat code system: a <code>CodeSystem</code> with <code>hierarchyMeaning</code> of <code>is-a</code> and no nesting says nothing by putting one code before another. <b>32 tables carry exactly THO's codes in a different order.</b> If order is a change under the artifact versioning policy, those 32 all increment &mdash; and they increment again every time the chapter is re-laid-out, which is a version number spent on typesetting.</p><p class="ask"><b>The ask:</b> Confirm that concept order is not a versionable change, or say that it is. Either answer is one line in this project's comparison. The question is asked because the policy's element table lists <code>CodeSystem.concept (and all subelements)</code> without qualification, and a literal reading could be taken to cover sequence.</p>
  <div class="ri-who">Ruling: <p><b>TSMG</b> &mdash; Terminology Infrastructure WG meeting, HL7 Plenary, Rockville, 2026-09-21.</p><p><b>Ruling:</b> Reordering a code system's concepts is not a change, and does not increment the version.</p><p><b>Effect here:</b> None. The comparison already compared concepts as a set keyed by code, so no artifact moved and no version number changed. The 32 tables carrying exactly THO's codes in a different order keep THO's version on the policy owner's authority rather than on this project's reading of the policy.</p></div>
</div>

  <div class="cell">This table includes only simple somatic (cancer) mutations, one per unique mutation ID. The codes is the COSMIC mutation ID, and the name uses Ensembl RefSeqs and the single letter code for p.HGVS. It carries fields analogous to most of the key fields in ClinVar, but its reference sequences are Ensembl transcript reference sequences with prefixes of ENST; it specifies amino acid changes with the older, HGVS, single letter codes and it carries examples of primary cancers and primary tissues, fields that are not in ClinVar. COSMIC&#x27;s source table includes multiple records per mutation - one per submission. The COSMIC-Simple Variants table carries only includes one record per unique mutation- more than 3 million of them. These contents are copyright COSMIC (http://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/cosmic/license) LHC has produced a look up table for these records, and for users to look up particular mutation IDs with permission from COSMIC. However, interested parties must contact COSMIC for permission to download these records.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0467</div>
  <div class="cell">The OPPS functionality of the Integrated Outpatient Code Editor (I/OCE) software was developed for the implementation of the Medicare outpatient prospective payment system mandated by the 1997 Balanced Budget Act. CMS released the proposed OPPS rules using the Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) system in the September 8, 1998 Federal Register. Final regulations were published in the April 7, 2000 Federal Register and the system became effective for Medicare on August 1, 2000.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the GP1 segment.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The APC-based OPPS developed by CMS is the outpatient equivalent of the inpatient, DRG-based PPS. The APC system establishes groups of covered services so that the services within each group are comparable clinically and with respect to the use of resources.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Hospitals are required to use HCPCS when billing for outpatient services.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The OCE not only identifies individual errors but also indicates what actions should be taken and the reasons why these actions are necessary. In order to accommodate this functionality, the OCE is structured to return lists of edit numbers. This structure facilitates the linkage between the actions being taken, the reasons for the actions and the information on the claim (e.g., a specific diagnosis) that caused the action. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>In general, the OCE performs all functions that require specific reference to HCPCS codes, HCPCS modifiers and ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes (ICD-9-CM diagnosis codes for historical claims with From Dates prior to 10/1/2015). Since these coding systems are complex and annually updated, the centralization of the direct reference to these codes and modifiers in a single program reduces effort and reduces the chance of inconsistent processing.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>This is a CMS maintained list of edits: Please see the following for additional information: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/index.html<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/Background.htmlC<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/OCEQtrReleaseSpecs.html</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">The OPPS functionality of the Integrated Outpatient Code Editor (I/OCE) software was developed for the implementation of the Medicare outpatient prospective payment system mandated by the 1997 Balanced Budget Act. CMS released the proposed OPPS rules using the Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) system in the September 8, 1998 Federal Register. Final regulations were published in the April 7, 2000 Federal Register and the system became effective for Medicare on August 1, 2000. Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the GP1 segment.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The APC-based OPPS developed by CMS is the outpatient equivalent of the inpatient, DRG-based PPS. The APC system establishes groups of covered services so that the services within each group are comparable clinically and with respect to the use of resources.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Hospitals are required to use HCPCS when billing for outpatient services.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The OCE not only identifies individual errors but also indicates what actions should be taken and the reasons why these actions are necessary. <div class="ri-item ri-resolved">

  <div class="cell">A code specifying the particular kind of Act that the Act-instance represents within its class.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Constraints: The kind of Act (e.g. physical examination, serum potassium, inpatient encounter, charge financial transaction, etc.) is specified with a code from one of several, typically external, coding systems. The coding system will depend on the class of Act, such as LOINC for observations, etc.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Conceptually, the Act.code must be a specialization of the Act.classCode. This is why the structure of ActClass domain should be reflected in the superstructure of the ActCode domain and then individual codes or externally referenced vocabularies subordinated under these domains that reflect the ActClass structure.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Act.classCode and Act.code are not modifiers of each other but the Act.code concept should really imply the Act.classCode concept. For a negative example, it is not appropriate to use an Act.code &quot;potassium&quot; together with and Act.classCode for &quot;laboratory observation&quot; to somehow mean &quot;potassium laboratory observation&quot; and then use the same Act.code for &quot;potassium&quot; together with Act.classCode for &quot;medication&quot; to mean &quot;substitution of potassium&quot;. This mutually modifying use of Act.code and Act.classCode is not permitted.Code system of concepts specifying the reason for the restricted access.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the ARV segment.</div>

  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">can be associated with one or more OM4 (specimen) segments<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Codes P, F, and S identify sets (batteries) and should be associated with an OM5 segment that defines the list of elements.   <div class="cell">IEEE 64-bit Extended Unique Identifier is comprised of a<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>24-bit company identifier and a 40-bit instance identifier.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The value shall be formatted as 16 ASCII HEX digits, for example, “AABBCC1122334455”.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The 24-bit company identifier, formally known as Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI-24), is guaranteed to be globally unique.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The 40-bit extensions are assigned by manufacturers.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>This identifier is often used in equipment interfaces (e.g., “MAC” address format for IPv4 &amp; IPv6).<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>[See http://standards.ieee.org/regauth/oui/tutorials/EUI64.htmlfor a detailed explanation of the format.]OUI-24 values are administered by the IEEE Registration Authority.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">IEEE 64-bit Extended Unique Identifier is comprised of a<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>24-bit company identifier and a 40-bit instance identifier. The value shall be formatted as 16 ASCII HEX digits, for example, “AABBCC1122334455”. The 24-bit company identifier, formally known as Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI-24), is guaranteed to be globally unique. The 40-bit extensions are assigned by manufacturers. This identifier is often used in equipment interfaces (e.g., “MAC” address format for IPv4 &amp; IPv6). [See http://standards.ieee.org/regauth/oui/tutorials/EUI64.htmlfor a detailed explanation of the format.]OUI-24 values are administered by the IEEE Registration Authority.</div></div>
</div>

  <div class="cell">Each code in this system represents a single line in a database template for the College of American Pathologists Electronic Cancer Checklist (CAP eCC).<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Each line and its code corresponds to either a question or an answer selection.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The code is in a decimal format of #########.#########, where each &quot;#&quot; is an optional number.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The nine digits to the right of the Ckey decimal point make up a namespace identifier, which is specific to the center that created the database entries for the checklist line items with their unique Ckey values.<span class="ws" title="3 spaces">&middot;&middot;&middot;</span>The namespace identifier for SNOMED Terminology Solutions at the College of American Pathologists is 1000043.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>All Ckey values in the 2008 release use namespace 1000043.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The digits to the left of the decimal point are a locally assigned sequential key for the ChecklistTemplateItems table in the local CAP eCC database.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>These codes are used to specify questions and answers selected in a CAP eCC template for transmission in an HL7 message, as defined by the NAACCR Pathology Workgroup and the CDC/NPCR Reporting Pathology Protocols II (RPP II) project. SNOMED Terminology Solutions, College of American Pathologists, 325 Waukegan Road, Northfield, Illinois, 60093, snomedsolutions@cap.org</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">Each code in this system represents a single line in a database template for the College of American Pathologists Electronic Cancer Checklist (CAP eCC). Each line and its code corresponds to either a question or an answer selection. The code is in a decimal format of #########.#########, where each &quot;#&quot; is an optional number. The nine digits to the right of the Ckey decimal point make up a namespace identifier, which is specific to the center that created the database entries for the checklist line items with their unique Ckey values. The namespace identifier for SNOMED Terminology Solutions at the College of American Pathologists is 1000043. All Ckey values in the 2008 release use namespace 1000043. The digits to the left of the decimal point are a locally assigned sequential key for the ChecklistTemplateItems table in the local CAP eCC database. These codes are used to specify questions and answers selected in a CAP eCC template for transmission in an HL7 message, as defined by the NAACCR Pathology Workgroup and the CDC/NPCR Reporting Pathology Protocols II (RPP II) project. SNOMED Terminology Solutions, College of American Pathologists, 325 Waukegan Road, Northfield, Illinois, 60093, snomedsolutions@cap.org</div></div>
</div>

  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">This table includes only simple somatic (cancer) mutations, one per unique mutation ID. </div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">

  <div class="cell">Identifies an address for mail correspondence from a healthcare provider as stipulated by the subject.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>For example, under the tenets of certain privacy regulations, it is exclusive to the patient and is typically maintained at the encounter or visit level versus the person level as it only has relevance to the specifics of a given encounter.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>This is an exception category of address in that the patient has stipulated that they want all correspondence relevant to a given encounter sent to this address in lieu of any other address on file.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Providers are required to accommodate such requests under HIPAA promulgated regulation.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Note that mailing and legal address may be mutually exclusive as defined below.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>(Implementors are reminded that although the privacy regulation requires the provider to honor such requests, it does require the provider to enquire whether the patient has a preferred address other than the one volunteered.)</div>

[https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.501].<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Also see HHS Individuals’ Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information 45 CFR Section 164.524 [https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/access/index.html#maximumflatfee].</div></div>
</div>

  <div class="cell">A consent directive compliant with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) definition: Consent of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data subject’s wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If the data subject’s consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Any part of such a declaration which constitutes an infringement of this Regulation shall not be binding.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time. The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Prior to giving consent, the data subject shall be informed thereof. It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>When assessing whether consent is freely given, utmost account shall be taken of whether, inter alia, the performance of a contract, including the provision of a service, is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Consent should be given by a clear or inactivity should not therefore constitute consent. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Consent should cover all processing </div>

  <div class="cell">HL7-defined table of codes used to specify the interpretation for the blood product observation status codes.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>A status is considered preliminary until a blood product has reached a final disposition for the patient. When the product is dispensed to the patient, that status would also be considered preliminary.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>However, once the product is transfused, the status would be considered final.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">HL7-defined table of codes used to specify the interpretation for the blood product observation status codes. When the product is dispensed to the patient, that status would also be considered preliminary. However, once the product is transfused, the status would be considered final.</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0513</div>
  <div class="cell">HL7-defined code system of concepts used to specify the current status of the specified blood product as indicated by the placer. For example, the placer may return the blood product to the transfusion service unused because an IV could not be started. The blood component may have been entered, but the line was clogged and could not be used, in which case the component must be wasted. A final status would indicate that the product has actually been &quot;transfused.&quot;<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in the Blood Product Transfusion/Disposition (BTX) segment in HL7 Version 2.x messaging.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">HL7-defined code system of concepts used to specify the current status of the specified blood product as indicated by the placer. For example, the placer may return the blood product to the transfusion service unused because an IV could not be started. The blood component may have been entered, but the line was clogged and could not be used, in which case the component must be wasted. A final status would indicate that the product has actually been &quot;transfused.&quot; Used in the Blood Product Transfusion/Disposition (BTX) segment in HL7 Version 2.x messaging.</div></div>
</div>

  <div class="cell">Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) including modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note: The HCPCS code is divided into three &quot;levels.&quot;<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Level I includes the entire CPT-4 code by reference. Level II includes the American Dental Association’s Current Dental Terminology (CDT-2) code by reference. Level II also includes the genuine HCPCS codes, approved and maintained jointly by the Alpha-Numeric Editorial Panel, consisting of CMS, the Health Insurance Association of America, and the Blue Cross and Blue Shield Association. Level III are codes developed locally by Medicare carriers. The HCPCS modifiers are divided into the same three levels, I being CPT-4 modifiers, II CDT-2 and genuine HCPCS modifiers, and III being locally agreed modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The genuine HCPCS codes and modifiers of level II can be found at http://www.hcfa.gov/stats/anhcpcdl.htm. CMS distributes the HCPCS codes via the National Technical Information Service (NTIS, www.ntis.gov) and NTIS distribution includes the CDT-2 part of HCPCS Level II, but does not include the CPT-4 part (Level I). CMS may distribute the CPT-4 part to ist contractors.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <div class="cell">A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule (45 CFR Section 164.522), which stipulates the process by which a covered entity seeks agreement from an individual regarding how it will use and disclose the individual&#x27;s protected health information for treatment, payment, and health care operations is termed a &quot;consent.&quot;<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The Privacy Rule permits, but does not require, a covered entity to voluntarily obtain patient consent for uses and disclosures of protected health information for treatment, payment, and health care operations. Covered entities that do so have complete discretion to design a process that best suits their needs. From https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/264/what-is-the-difference-between-consent-and-authorization/index.html. The provisions relating to consent are largely contained in<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Section 164.522 Rights to request privacy protection for protected health information https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-522.pdf</div>

Covered entities that do so have complete discretion to design a process that best suits their needs. From https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/264/what-is-the-difference-between-consent-and-authorization/index.html. The provisions relating to consent are largely contained in<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Section 164.522 Rights to request privacy protection for protected health information https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-522.pdf</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0396</div>
  <div class="cell">Chromosome location (AKA chromosome locus or cytogenetic location), is the standardized syntax for recording the position of genes and large mutations. It consists of three parts: the Chromosome number (e 1-22, X, Y), an indicator of which arm – either “p” for the short or “q” for the long, and then a series of numbers separated by dots that indicate the band, sub band and sub-sub band of the locus - e.g., 2p16.3 . There are other conventions for reporting ranges and locations at the end of the chromosomes. The table of these chromosome locations was loaded initially with the all of the locations found in NCBI’s ClinVar variation tables. It will expand as additional sources become available.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">Chromosome location (AKA chromosome locus or cytogenetic location), is the standardized syntax for recording the position of genes and large mutations. It consists of three parts: the Chromosome number (e 1-22, X, Y), an indicator of which arm – either “p” for the short or “q” for the long, and then a series of numbers separated by dots that indicate the band, sub band and sub-sub band of the locus - e.g., 2p16.3. There are other conventions for reporting ranges and locations at the end of the chromosomes. The table of these chromosome locations was loaded initially with the all of the locations found in NCBI’s ClinVar variation tables. It will expand as additional sources become available.</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0952</div>
  <div class="cell">Types of privacy metadata classifying an IT resource (data, information object, service, or system capability) according to its level of sensitivity, which is based on an analysis of applicable privacy policies and the risk of financial, reputational, or other harm to an individual or entity that could result if made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note : Confidentiality codes may be used in security labels and privacy markings to classify IT resources based on sensitivity to indicate the obligation of a custodian or receiver to ensure that the protected resource is not made available or disclosed to individuals, entities, or processes (security principals) unless authorized per applicable policies. Confidentiality codes may also be used in the clearances of initiators requesting access to protected resources.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map: Definition aligns with ISO 7498-2:1989 - Confidentiality is the property that information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">Types of privacy metadata classifying an IT resource (data, information object, service, or system capability) according to its level of sensitivity, which is based on an analysis of applicable privacy policies and the risk of financial, reputational, or other harm to an individual or entity that could result if made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note: Confidentiality codes may be used in security labels and privacy markings to classify IT resources based on sensitivity to indicate the obligation of a custodian or receiver to ensure that the protected resource is not made available or disclosed to individuals, entities, or processes (security principals) unless authorized per applicable policies. Confidentiality codes may also be used in the clearances of initiators requesting access to protected resources.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map: Definition aligns with ISO 7498-2:1989 - Confidentiality is the property that information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes</div></div>

Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the Test Code Detail (TCD) segment.</div>

  <div class="cell">A code specifying the particular kind of Act that the Act-instance represents within its class.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Constraints: The kind of Act (e.g. physical examination, serum potassium, inpatient encounter, charge financial transaction, etc.) is specified with a code from one of several, typically external, coding systems. For a negative example, it is not appropriate to use an Act.code &quot;potassium&quot; together with and Act.classCode for &quot;laboratory observation&quot; to somehow mean &quot;potassium laboratory observation&quot; and then use the same Act.code for &quot;potassium&quot; together with Act.classCode for &quot;medication&quot; to mean &quot;substitution of potassium&quot;. This mutually modifying use of Act.code and Act.classCode is not permitted.Code system of concepts specifying the reason for the restricted access. This mutually modifying use of Act.code and Act.classCode is not permitted.Code system of concepts specifying the reason for the restricted access. Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the ARV segment.</div></div>
</div>

There are other conventions for reporting ranges and locations at the end of the chromosomes.   <div class="cell">A code specifying the particular kind of Act that the Act-instance represents within its class.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Constraints: The kind of Act (e.g., physical examination, serum potassium, inpatient encounter, charge financial transaction, etc.) is specified with a code from one of several, typically external, coding systems. This is why the structure of ActClass domain should be reflected in the superstructure of the ActCode domain and then individual codes or externally referenced vocabularies subordinated under these domains that reflect the ActClass structure.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Act.classCode and Act.code are not modifiers of each other but the Act.code concept should really imply the Act.classCode concept. For a negative example, it is not appropriate to use an Act.code &quot;potassium&quot; together with and Act.classCode for &quot;laboratory observation&quot; to somehow mean &quot;potassium laboratory observation&quot; and then use the same Act.code for &quot;potassium&quot; together with Act.classCode for &quot;medication&quot; to mean &quot;substitution of potassium&quot;. This mutually modifying use of Act.code and Act.classCode is not permitted.Code system of concepts specifying the reason for the restricted access. Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the ARV segment.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">A code specifying the particular kind of Act that the Act-instance represents within its class.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Constraints: The kind of Act (e.g., physical examination, serum potassium, inpatient encounter, charge financial transaction, etc.) is specified with a code from one of several, typically external, coding systems. The coding system will depend on the class of Act, such as LOINC for observations, etc.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Conceptually, the Act.code must be a specialization of the Act.classCode. This is why the structure of ActClass domain should be reflected in the superstructure of the ActCode domain and then individual codes or externally referenced vocabularies subordinated under these domains that reflect the ActClass structure.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Act.classCode and Act.code are not modifiers of each other but the Act.code concept should really imply the Act.classCode concept. For a negative example, it is not appropriate to use an Act.code &quot;potassium&quot; together with and Act.classCode for &quot;laboratory observation&quot; to somehow mean &quot;potassium laboratory observation&quot; and then use the same Act.code for &quot;potassium&quot; together with Act.classCode for &quot;medication&quot; to mean &quot;substitution of potassium&quot;.   <div class="cell">RxNorm provides standard names for clinical drugs (active ingredient + strength + dose form) and for dose forms as administered to a patient. It provides links from clinical drugs, both branded and generic, to their active ingredients, drug components (active ingredient + strength), and related brand names. NDCs (National Drug Codes) for specific drug products (where there are often many NDC codes for a single product) are linked to that product in RxNorm. RxNorm links its names to many of the drug vocabularies commonly used in pharmacy management and drug interaction software, including those of First Databank, Micromedex, MediSpan, and Multum. By providing links between these vocabularies, RxNorm can mediate messages between systems not using the same software and vocabulary.RxNorm is one of a suite of designated standards for use in U.S. Federal Government systems for the electronic exchange of clinical health information.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">RxNorm provides standard names for clinical drugs (active ingredient + strength + dose form) and for dose forms as administered to a patient. NDCs (National Drug Codes) for specific drug products (where there are often many NDC codes for a single product) are linked to that product in RxNorm. RxNorm links its names to many of the drug vocabularies commonly used in pharmacy management and drug interaction software, including those of First Databank, Micromedex, MediSpan, and Multum. By providing links between these vocabularies, RxNorm can mediate messages between systems not using the same software and vocabulary. RxNorm is one of a suite of designated standards for use in U.S. Federal Government systems for the electronic exchange of clinical health information.</div></div>
</div>

#### Text changed: non breaking space in text &mdash; valueSet.Description <span class="ri-count">&mdash; 1 item</span>

<div class="ri-blurb">A run of non-breaking spaces in text became one ordinary space, per ADR-0008 D7. Where lines break is the renderer's decision in a FHIR resource, so a non-breaking space carries nothing.  These were changed.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0827</div>
  <div class="cell">This value set defines a base set of codes for country, country subdivision and region for indicating where a resource is intended to be used.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Note: The codes for countries and country subdivisions are taken from<span class="ws" title="non-breaking space">&#9251;</span>ISO 3166<span class="ws" title="non-breaking space">&#9251;</span><span class="ws" title="non-breaking space">&#9251;</span>while the codes for &quot;supra-national&quot; regions are from<span class="ws" title="non-breaking space">&#9251;</span>UN Standard country or area codes for statistical use (M49).</div>

#### Text changed: private use area character &mdash; conceptDomain.Description <span class="ri-count">&mdash; 1 item</span>

<div class="ri-blurb">A Symbol-font glyph from the Unicode private use area, deleted per ADR-0008 D7. It renders as a box or nothing at all outside the font it was typed in. The tab after it is kept, so the line reads as the indented list item it was meant to be.  These were changed.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0301</div>
  <div class="cell">IEEE 64-bit Extended Unique Identifier is comprised of a<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>24-bit company identifier and a 40-bit instance identifier. The value shall be formatted as 16 ASCII HEX digits, for example, “AABBCC1122334455”. The 24-bit company identifier, formally known as Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI-24), is guaranteed to be globally unique. The 40-bit extensions are assigned by manufacturers. This identifier is often used in equipment interfaces (e.g., “MAC” address format for IPv4 &amp; IPv6). [See http://standards.ieee.org/regauth/oui/tutorials/EUI64.htmlfor a detailed explanation of the format.]OUI-24 values are administered by the IEEE Registration Authority.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0396</div>
  <div class="cell">Chromosome location (AKA chromosome locus or cytogenetic location), is the standardized syntax for recording the position of genes and large mutations. It consists of three parts: the Chromosome number (e 1-22, X, Y), an indicator of which arm – either “p” for the<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>short or “q” for the long, and then a series of numbers separated by dots that indicate the band, sub band and sub-sub band of the locus - e.g. 2p16.3 . There are other conventions for reporting ranges and locations at the end of the chromosomes. The table of these chromosome locations was loaded initially with the all of the locations found in NCBI’s ClinVar variation tables. It will expand as additional sources become available.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">Chromosome location (AKA chromosome locus or cytogenetic location), is the standardized syntax for recording the position of genes and large mutations. It consists of three parts: the Chromosome number (e 1-22, X, Y), an indicator of which arm – either “p” for the short or “q” for the long, and then a series of numbers separated by dots that indicate the band, sub band and sub-sub band of the locus - e.g. 2p16.3 . There are other conventions for reporting ranges and locations at the end of the chromosomes. The table of these chromosome locations was loaded initially with the all of the locations found in NCBI’s ClinVar variation tables. It will expand as additional sources become available.</div></div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <div class="cell">This code is for backwards compatibility only as of v2.9. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If no restrictions, don’t send an ARV segment altogether. If sent, ARV-3 is a required element however. To emulate 0717 “NONE”, populate ARV-3 with code from new ActCode_ActPolicyType__ActInformationPolicy such as OrgNSI (organizational non-sensitive information policy) or PersNSI (personal non-sensitive information policy). <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Don’t populate ARV-7. E.g., Device record that is not sensitive. If you have a situation where an ARV-4 is valued, as required by, e.g., an organizational policy related to disclosure of<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>a VIP’s health status or location at a facility, and the VIP has authorized disclosure as public information, one may use OrgPI (organizational public information policy - Organizational policy on collection, access, use, or disclosure of public information as defined by the organization or governing jurisdiction) to value ARV-3 indicating that the policy permits the disclosure of VIP sensitive information as coded in ARV-4.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">This code is for backwards compatibility only as of v2.9. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If no restrictions, don’t send an ARV segment altogether. To emulate 0717 “NONE”, populate ARV-3 with code from new ActCode_ActPolicyType__ActInformationPolicy such as OrgNSI (organizational non-sensitive information policy) or PersNSI (personal non-sensitive information policy). <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Don’t populate ARV-7. E.g., Device record that is not sensitive. If you have a situation where an ARV-4 is valued, as required by, e.g., an organizational policy related to disclosure of a VIP’s health status or location at a facility, and the VIP has authorized disclosure as public information, one may use OrgPI (organizational public information policy - Organizational policy on collection, access, use, or disclosure of public information as defined by the organization or governing jurisdiction) to value ARV-3 indicating that the policy permits the disclosure of VIP sensitive information as coded in ARV-4.</div></div>
</div>

  <div class="cell">Implied consent with no opportunity to assent or dissent to certain terms is considered &quot;&quot;basic consent&quot;&quot;.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Examples: (1) Healthcare: (a) A patient schedules an appointment with a provider, and either does not take the opportunity to expressly assent or dissent to the provider&#x27;s consent<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>directive, does not have an opportunity to do so, as in the case where emergency care is required, or simply behaves as though the patient [grantor] agrees to the rights granted to the provider [grantee] in an implicit consent directive. (b) An injured and unconscious patient is deemed to have assented to emergency treatment by those permitted to do so under jurisdictional laws, e.g., Good Samaritan laws. (2) Non-healthcare: (a) Upon receiving a driver&#x27;s license, the driver is deemed to have assented without explicitly consenting to undergoing field sobriety tests. (b) A corporation that does business in a foreign nation is deemed to have deemed to have assented without explicitly consenting to abide by that nation&#x27;s laws.</div>

  <div class="cell">IEEE 64-bit Extended Unique Identifier is comprised of a<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>24-bit company identifier and a 40-bit instance identifier. The value shall be formatted as 16 ASCII HEX digits, for example, “AABBCC1122334455”. The 24-bit company identifier, formally known as Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI-24), is guaranteed to be globally unique. The 40-bit extensions are assigned by manufacturers. This identifier is often used in equipment interfaces (e.g., “MAC” address format for IPv4 &amp; IPv6). [See http://standards.ieee.org/regauth/oui/tutorials/EUI64.html for a detailed explanation of the format.]</div>
