<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <div class="cell">A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule (45 CFR Section 164.508), which stipulates the privacy rights of an individual who is the subject of psychotherapy notes, and requires authorization for certain uses and disclosure of that information.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Definition of Psychotherapy notes 45 CFR<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Section 164.501 https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-501.pdf: Psychotherapy notes means notes recorded (in any medium) by a health care provider who is a mental health professional documenting or analyzing the contents of conversation during a private counseling session or a group, joint, or family counseling session and that are separated from the rest of the individual&#x27;s medical record. Psychotherapy notes excludes medication prescription and monitoring, counseling session start and stop times, the modalities and frequencies of treatment furnished, results of clinical tests, and any summary of the following items: Diagnosis, functional status, the treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, and progress to date. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>See Section 164.508 Uses and disclosures for which an authorization is required. (2)Authorization required: Psychotherapy notes https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-508.pdf: Notwithstanding any provision of this subpart, other than the transition provisions in<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Section 164.532, a covered entity must obtain an authorization for any use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes, except: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(i) To carry out the following treatment, payment, or health care operations: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(A) Use by the originator of the psychotherapy notes for treatment; <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(B) Use or disclosure by the covered entity for its own training programs in which students, trainees, or practitioners in mental health learn under supervision to practice or improve their skills in group, joint, family, or individual counseling; or <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(C) Use or disclosure by the covered entity to defend itself in a legal action or other proceeding brought by the individual; and <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(ii) A use or disclosure that is required by Section 164.502(a)(2)(ii) or permitted by Section 164.512(a); Section 164.512(d) with respect to the oversight of the originator of the psychotherapy notes;<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Section 164.512(g)(1);<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Section 164.512(j)(1)(i).</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <div class="cell">A code representing Title 38 Section 7332, which is a US Federal law stipulating the privacy rights of veterans diagnosed and treated for substance use disorders, infection with the human immunodeficiency virus, or sickle cell anemia.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Title 38 Section 7332 - Confidentiality of certain medical records<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/granule/USCODE-2011-title38/USCODE-2011-title38-partV-chap73-subchapIII-sec7332/content-detail.html<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(1) Records of the identity, diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment of any patient or subject which are maintained in connection with the performance of any program or activity (including education, training, treatment, rehabilitation, or research) relating to drug abuse, alcoholism or alcohol abuse, infection with the human immunodeficiency virus, or sickle cell anemia which is carried out by or for the Department under this title shall, except as provided in subsections (e) and (f), be confidential, and (section 5701 of this title to the contrary notwithstanding) such records may be disclosed only for the purposes and under the circumstances expressly authorized under subsection (b).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(2) Paragraph (1) prohibits the disclosure to any person or entity other than the patient or subject concerned of the fact that a special written consent is required in order for such records to be disclosed.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(b) (1) The content of any record referred to in subsection (a) may be disclosed by the Secretary in accordance with the prior written consent of the patient or subject with respect to whom such record is maintained, but only to such extent, under such circumstances, and for such purposes as may be allowed in regulations prescribed by the Secretary.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(2) Whether or not any patient or subject, with respect to whom any given record referred to in subsection (a) is maintained, gives written consent, the content of such record may be disclosed by the Secretary as follows: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(A) To medical personnel to the extent necessary to meet a bona fide medical emergency.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(B) To qualified personnel for the purpose of conducting scientific research, management audits, financial audits, or program evaluation, but such personnel may not identify, directly or indirectly, any individual patient or subject in any report of such research, audit, or evaluation, or otherwise disclose patient or subject identities in any manner.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(C) (i) In the case of any record which is maintained in connection with the performance of any program or activity relating to infection with the human immunodeficiency virus, to a Federal, State, or local public-health authority charged under Federal or State law with the protection of the public health, and to which Federal or State law requires disclosure of such record, if a qualified representative of such authority has made a written request that such record be provided as required pursuant to such law for a purpose authorized by such law.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(ii) A person to whom a record is disclosed under this paragraph may not redisclose or use such record for a purpose other than that for which the disclosure was made.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(D) If authorized by an appropriate order of a court of competent jurisdiction granted after application showing good cause therefor. In assessing good cause the court shall weigh the public interest and the need for disclosure against the injury to the patient or subject, to the physician-patient relationship, and to the treatment services. Upon the granting of such order, the court, in determining the extent to which any disclosure of all or any part of any record is necessary, shall impose appropriate safeguards against unauthorized disclosure.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(E) To an entity described in paragraph (1)(B) of section 5701(k) of this title, but only to the extent authorized by such section.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(F) (i) To a representative of a patient who lacks decision-making capacity, when a practitioner deems the content of the given record necessary for that representative to make an informed decision regarding the patient’s treatment.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(ii) In this subparagraph, the term “representative” means an individual, organization, or other body authorized under section 7331 of this title and its implementing regulations to give informed consent on behalf of a patient who lacks decision-making capacity.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(G) To a State controlled substance monitoring program, including a program approved by the Secretary of Health and Human Services under section 399O of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 280g–3), to the extent necessary to prevent misuse and diversion of prescription medicines.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(H) (i) To a non-Department entity (including private entities and other Federal agencies) for purposes of providing health care, including hospital care, medical services, and extended care services, to Veterans or performing other health care-related activities or functions. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(ii) An entity to which a record is disclosed under this subparagraph may not disclose or use such record for a purpose other than that for which the disclosure was made or as permitted by law.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(I) To a third party in order to recover or collect reasonable charges for care furnished to, or paid on behalf of, a Veteran in connection with a non-service connected disability as permitted by section 1729 of this title or for a condition for which recovery is authorized or with respect to which the United States is deemed to be a third party beneficiary under the Act entitled ‘An Act to provide for the recovery from tortiously liable third persons of the cost of hospital and medical care and treatment furnished by the United States’ (Public Law 87–693; 42 U.S.C. 2651 et seq.; commonly known as the ‘Federal Medical Care Recovery Act’).</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <div class="cell">A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule (45 CFR Section 164.522), which stipulates the process by which a covered entity seeks agreement from an individual regarding how it will use and disclose the individual&#x27;s protected health information for treatment, payment, and health care operations is termed a &quot;consent.&quot; The Privacy Rule permits, but does not require, a covered entity to voluntarily obtain patient consent for uses and disclosures of protected health information for treatment, payment, and health care operations. Covered entities that do so have complete discretion to design a process that best suits their needs. From https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/264/what-is-the-difference-between-consent-and-authorization/index.html. The provisions relating to consent are largely contained in<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Section 164.522 Rights to request privacy protection for protected health information https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-522.pdf</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule (45 CFR Section 164.522), which stipulates the process by which a covered entity seeks agreement from an individual regarding how it will use and disclose the individual&#x27;s protected health information for treatment, payment, and health care operations is termed a &quot;consent.&quot; The Privacy Rule permits, but does not require, a covered entity to voluntarily obtain patient consent for uses and disclosures of protected health information for treatment, payment, and health care operations. Covered entities that do so have complete discretion to design a process that best suits their needs. From https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/264/what-is-the-difference-between-consent-and-authorization/index.html. The provisions relating to consent are largely contained in Section 164.522 Rights to request privacy protection for protected health information https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-522.pdf</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-resolved">
  <div class="ri-key">0078</div>
  <div class="cell">A categorical assessment, providing a rough qualitative interpretation of the observation value, such as “normal”/ “abnormal”,”low” / “high”, “better” / “worse”, “susceptible” / “resistant”, “expected”/ “not expected”. The value set is intended to be for ANY use where coded representation of an interpretation is needed. Notes: This is being communicated in v2.x in OBX-8, in v3 in ObservationInterpretation (CWE) in R1 (Representative Realm) and in FHIR Observation.interpretation. Historically these values come from the laboratory domain, and these codes are extensively used. The value set binding is extensible, so codes outside the value set that are needed for interpretation concepts<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>(i.e. particular meanings) that are not included in the value set can be used, and these new codes may also be added to the value set and published in a future version.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted: <div class="cell">A categorical assessment, providing a rough qualitative interpretation of the observation value, such as “normal”/ “abnormal”,”low” / “high”, “better” / “worse”, “susceptible” / “resistant”, “expected”/ “not expected”. The value set is intended to be for ANY use where coded representation of an interpretation is needed. Notes: This is being communicated in v2.x in OBX-8, in v3 in ObservationInterpretation (CWE) in R1 (Representative Realm) and in FHIR Observation.interpretation. Historically these values come from the laboratory domain, and these codes are extensively used. The value set binding is extensible, so codes outside the value set that are needed for interpretation concepts (i.e. particular meanings) that are not included in the value set can be used, and these new codes may also be added to the value set and published in a future version.</div></div>

#### Concept domains &mdash; Definition differs from tho editorially <span class="ri-count">&mdash; 1 item</span>

<div class="ri-blurb">Chapter 2C and THO use the same words in the same order and differ only in punctuation or markup. THO's wording was kept. Listed so the difference is visible, but there is nothing here to adjudicate.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key"><code>Confidentiality</code></div>
  0952
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Types of privacy metadata classifying an IT resource (data, information object, service, or system capability) according to its level of sensitivity, which is based on an analysis of applicable privacy policies and the risk of financial, reputational, or other harm to an individual or entity that could result if made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note:</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Confidentiality codes may be used in security labels and privacy markings to classify IT resources based on sensitivity to indicate the obligation of a custodian or receiver to ensure that the protected resource is not made available or disclosed to individuals, entities, or processes (security principals) unless authorized per applicable policies. Confidentiality codes may also be used in the clearances of initiators requesting access to protected resources.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map:</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Definition aligns with ISO 7498-2:1989 - Confidentiality is the property that information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">processes</span></div>
  <div class="ri-who">THO: <div class="cell">Types of privacy metadata classifying an IT resource (data, information object, service, or system capability) according to its level of sensitivity, which is based on an analysis of applicable privacy policies and the risk of financial, reputational, or other harm to an individual or entity that could result if made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>*Usage Note:*</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Confidentiality codes may be used in security labels and privacy markings to classify IT resources based on sensitivity to indicate the obligation of a custodian or receiver to ensure that the protected resource is not made available or disclosed to individuals, entities, or processes (security principals) unless authorized per applicable policies. Confidentiality codes may also be used in the clearances of initiators requesting access to protected resources.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>*Map:*</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Definition aligns with ISO 7498-2:1989 - Confidentiality is the property that information is not made available or disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">processes.</span></div></div>

  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A code specifying the particular kind of Act that the Act-instance represents within its class.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Constraints: The kind of Act<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">(e.g.,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>physical examination, serum potassium, inpatient encounter, charge financial transaction, etc.) is specified with a code from one of several, typically external, coding systems. The coding system will depend on the class of Act, such as LOINC for observations, etc.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Conceptually, the Act.code must be a specialization of the Act.classCode. This is why the structure of ActClass domain should be reflected in the superstructure of the ActCode domain and then individual codes or externally referenced vocabularies subordinated under these domains that reflect the ActClass structure.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Act.classCode and Act.code are not modifiers of each other but the Act.code concept should really imply the Act.classCode concept. For a negative example, it is not appropriate to use an Act.code<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">&quot;potassium&quot; together with and Act.classCode for &quot;laboratory observation&quot; to somehow mean &quot;potassium laboratory observation&quot; and then use the same Act.code for &quot;potassium&quot; together with Act.classCode for &quot;medication&quot; to mean &quot;substitution of potassium&quot;. This mutually modifying use of Act.code and Act.classCode is not permitted. Code system of concepts specifying the reason for the restricted access. Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the ARV segment.</span></div>

</div>

  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Codes created by an organization as a shorthand way to express a combination of container attributes; for example the combination of SAC-47 (Container Form) of<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“Tube/vial” + SAC-48 (Container Material) of “Glass” + SAC-27 (Additive) of “EDTA” may be referenced commonly in an organization as a “Lavender Top”, e.g.:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Lavender Top<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Wet Mount (slides for parasitology)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>LJ plate (for Mycobacterium cultures)</span></div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">Codes created by an organization as a shorthand way to express a combination of container attributes; for example the combination of SAC-47 (Container Form) of<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in"><span class="empty">(empty)</span></span></div></div>

  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A categorical assessment, providing a rough qualitative interpretation of the observation value, such as<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“normal”/ “abnormal”,”low”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>/<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“high”, “better”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>/<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“worse”, “susceptible”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>/<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“resistant”, “expected”/ “not expected”.</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>The value set is intended to be for ANY use where coded representation of an interpretation is needed.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Notes: This is being communicated in v2.x in OBX-8, in v3 in ObservationInterpretation (CWE) in R1 (Representative Realm) and in FHIR Observation.interpretation.   <code>codedContent[8].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Refers to a special case address specific to the status of a subject or legal action involving the subject. For example, prisoners being treated at a healthcare facility may have home addresses, but their status mandates an address specific to their place of incarceration. In cases involving civil or criminal proceedings, a record may be flagged such that all correspondence is sent to any variety of legal entities.</div>

  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Use case: This is a registration number that identifies an individual or organization relative to controlled substance regulation and transactions. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>A DEA number has a very precise and widely accepted meaning within the United States. <div class="ri-item ri-informational">

  <code>codedContent[18].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Does not need an escape sequence.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>BIG-5 does not need an escape sequence. ASCII is a 7 bit character set, which means that the top bit of the byte is<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“0”.</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>The parser knows that when the top bit of the byte is<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“0”,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>the character set is ASCII. When it is<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“1”,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>the following bytes should be handled as 2 bytes (or more).   <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Table of codes used to indicate which adjustments should be made to a<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">guarantor’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>charges.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>For example, when a hospital agrees to adjust a<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">guarantor’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>charges to a sliding scale.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>No suggested values.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">Table of codes used to indicate which adjustments should be made to a<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">guarantor&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>charges.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>For example, when a hospital agrees to adjust a<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">guarantor&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>charges to a sliding scale.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>No suggested values.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0223</div>
  <code>codeSystems[0].Description</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>HL7-defined code system of concepts that identify specific living conditions (e.g., spouse dependent on patient, walk-up) that are relevant to an evaluation of the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">patient’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>healthcare needs.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>This information can be used for discharge planning.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Examples might include Spouse Dependent, Medical Supervision Required, Small Children Dependent.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Used in Version 2.s messaging in the NK1 segment.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">HL7-defined code system of concepts that identify specific living conditions (e.g., spouse dependent on patient, walk-up) that are relevant to an evaluation of the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">patient&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>healthcare needs.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>This information can be used for discharge planning.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>Examples might include Spouse Dependent, Medical Supervision Required, Small Children Dependent.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>Used in Version 2.s messaging in the NK1 segment.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0254</div>
  <code>codeSystems[0].Description</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>HL7 published code system of concepts that describe categories of an underlying kind of property represented by an observation.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>These are intended to distinguish concentrations from total amounts, molar concentrations from mass concentrations, partial pressures from colors, and so forth.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>These are discussed more fully in the LOINC<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">Users’</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Manual.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>These defined categories are derived from the approach described in 1995 edition of the IUPAC Silver Book.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>These distinctions are used in IUPAC and LOINC standard codes.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Needs review by OO and HTA to determined if this is a value set built on LOINC part codes or some other external vocabulary.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">HL7 published code system of concepts that describe categories of an underlying kind of property represented by an observation.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>These are intended to distinguish concentrations from total amounts, molar concentrations from mass concentrations, partial pressures from colors, and so forth.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>These are discussed more fully in the LOINC<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">Users&#x27;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Manual.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="3 spaces">&middot;&middot;&middot;</span></span>These defined categories are derived from the approach described in 1995 edition of the IUPAC Silver Book.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>These distinctions are used in IUPAC and LOINC standard codes.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>Needs review by OO and HTA to determined if this is a value set built on LOINC part codes or some other external vocabulary.</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0299</div>
  <code>codedContent[2].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Encoding as defined by MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) standard RFC 1521. Four consecutive ASCII characters represent three consecutive octets of binary data. Base64 utilizes a 65-character subset of US-ASCII, consisting of both the upper and lower case alphabetic characters, digits<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“0”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>through<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“9”,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“+”,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“/”,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>and<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“=”.</span></div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">Encoding as defined by MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) standard RFC 1521. Four consecutive ASCII characters represent three consecutive octets of binary data. Base64 utilizes a 65-character subset of US-ASCII, consisting of both the upper and lower case alphabetic characters, digits<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;0&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>through<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;9&quot;,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;+&quot;,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;/&quot;,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>and<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;=&quot;.</span></div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0301</div>
  <code>codedContent[4].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>IEEE 64-bit Extended Unique Identifier is comprised of a<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>24-bit company identifier and a 40-bit instance identifier.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>The value shall be formatted as 16 ASCII HEX digits, for example,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“AABBCC1122334455”.<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span></span>The 24-bit company identifier, formally known as Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI-24), is guaranteed to be globally unique.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>The 40-bit extensions are assigned by manufacturers.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>This identifier is often used in equipment interfaces (e.g.,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“MAC”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>address format for IPv4 &amp; IPv6).<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>[See http://standards.ieee.org/regauth/oui/tutorials/EUI64.html for a detailed explanation of the format.]</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">IEEE 64-bit Extended Unique Identifier is comprised of a<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>24-bit company identifier and a 40-bit instance identifier.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>The value shall be formatted as 16 ASCII HEX digits, for example,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;AABBCC1122334455&quot;.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>The 24-bit company identifier, formally known as Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI-24), is guaranteed to be globally unique.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>The 40-bit extensions are assigned by manufacturers.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>This identifier is often used in equipment interfaces (e.g.,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;MAC&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>address format for IPv4 &amp; IPv6).<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>[See http://standards.ieee.org/regauth/oui/tutorials/EUI64.html for a detailed explanation of the format.]</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0301</div>
  <code>codedContent[4].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>IEEE 64-bit Extended Unique Identifier is comprised of a<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>24-bit company identifier and a 40-bit instance identifier.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>The value shall be formatted as 16 ASCII HEX digits, for example,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“AABBCC1122334455”.<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span></span>The 24-bit company identifier, formally known as Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI-24), is guaranteed to be globally unique.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>The 40-bit extensions are assigned by manufacturers.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>This identifier is often used in equipment interfaces (e.g.,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“MAC”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>address format for IPv4 &amp; IPv6).<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>[See http://standards.ieee.org/regauth/oui/tutorials/EUI64.htmlfor a detailed explanation of the format.]OUI-24 values are administered by the IEEE Registration Authority.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">IEEE 64-bit Extended Unique Identifier is comprised of a<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>24-bit company identifier and a 40-bit instance identifier.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>The value shall be formatted as 16 ASCII HEX digits, for example,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;AABBCC1122334455&quot;.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>The 24-bit company identifier, formally known as Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI-24), is guaranteed to be globally unique.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>The 40-bit extensions are assigned by manufacturers.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>This identifier is often used in equipment interfaces (e.g.,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;MAC&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>address format for IPv4 &amp; IPv6).<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>[See http://standards.ieee.org/regauth/oui/tutorials/EUI64.htmlfor a detailed explanation of the format.]OUI-24 values are administered by the IEEE Registration Authority.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0340</div>
  <code>codedContent[1].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) including modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note: The HCPCS code is divided into three &quot;levels.&quot;<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Level I includes the entire CPT-4 code by reference.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Level II includes the American Dental<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">Association’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Current Dental Terminology (CDT-2) code by reference.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Level II also includes the genuine HCPCS codes, approved and maintained jointly by the Alpha-Numeric Editorial Panel, consisting of CMS, the Health Insurance Association of America, and the Blue Cross and Blue Shield Association. Level III are codes developed locally by Medicare carriers.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>The HCPCS modifiers are divided into the same three levels, I being CPT-4 modifiers, II CDT-2 and genuine HCPCS modifiers, and III being locally agreed modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The genuine HCPCS codes and modifiers of level II can be found at http://www.hcfa.gov/stats/anhcpcdl.htm. CMS distributes the HCPCS codes via the National Technical Information Service (NTIS, www.ntis.gov) and NTIS distribution includes the CDT-2 part of HCPCS Level II, but does not include the CPT-4 part (Level I). CMS may distribute the CPT-4 part to ist contractors.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) including modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note: The HCPCS code is divided into three &quot;levels.&quot;<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>Level I includes the entire CPT-4 code by reference.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>Level II includes the American Dental<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">Association&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Current Dental Terminology (CDT-2) code by reference.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>Level II also includes the genuine HCPCS codes, approved and maintained jointly by the Alpha-Numeric Editorial Panel, consisting of CMS, the Health Insurance Association of America, and the Blue Cross and Blue Shield Association. Level III are codes developed locally by Medicare carriers.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>The HCPCS modifiers are divided into the same three levels, I being CPT-4 modifiers, II CDT-2 and genuine HCPCS modifiers, and III being locally agreed modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The genuine HCPCS codes and modifiers of level II can be found at http://www.hcfa.gov/stats/anhcpcdl.htm. CMS distributes the HCPCS codes via the National Technical Information Service (NTIS, www.ntis.gov) and NTIS distribution includes the CDT-2 part of HCPCS Level II, but does not include the CPT-4 part (Level I). CMS may distribute the CPT-4 part to ist contractors.</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0356</div>
  <code>codedContent[0].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Note that the escape sequences used in this mode do not use the ASCII<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“esc”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>character, as defined in ISO 2022-1994.   <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Chromosome location (AKA chromosome locus or cytogenetic location), is the standardized syntax for recording the position of genes and large mutations. It consists of three parts: the Chromosome number (e 1-22, X, Y), an indicator of which arm – either<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“p” for the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span></span>short or<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“q”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>for the long, and then a series of numbers separated by dots that indicate the band, sub band and sub-sub band of the locus -<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">e.g., 2p16.3.</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>There are other conventions for reporting ranges and locations at the end of the chromosomes. It will expand as additional sources become available.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">

  <code>codedContent[11].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>This code is for backwards compatibility only as of v2.9. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If no restrictions,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">don’t</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>send an ARV segment altogether.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>If sent, ARV-3 is a required element however. To emulate 0717<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“NONE”,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>populate ARV-3 with code from new ActCode_ActPolicyType__ActInformationPolicy such as OrgNSI (organizational non-sensitive information policy) or PersNSI (personal non-sensitive information policy).<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Don’t</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>populate ARV-7.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>E.g., Device record that is not sensitive. If you have a situation where an ARV-4 is valued, as required by, e.g., an organizational policy related to disclosure of<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>a VIP’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>health status or location at a facility, and the VIP has authorized disclosure as public information, one may use OrgPI (organizational public information policy - Organizational policy on collection, access, use, or disclosure of public information as defined by the organization or governing jurisdiction) to value ARV-3 indicating that the policy permits the disclosure of VIP sensitive information as coded in ARV-4.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">This code is for backwards compatibility only as of v2.9. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If no restrictions,<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">don&#x27;t</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>send an ARV segment altogether.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>If sent, ARV-3 is a required element however. To emulate 0717<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;NONE&quot;,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>populate ARV-3 with code from new ActCode_ActPolicyType__ActInformationPolicy such as OrgNSI (organizational non-sensitive information policy) or PersNSI (personal non-sensitive information policy).<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="3 spaces">&middot;&middot;&middot;</span><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Don&#x27;t</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>populate ARV-7.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>E.g., Device record that is not sensitive. If you have a situation where an ARV-4 is valued, as required by, e.g., an organizational policy related to disclosure of<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>a VIP&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>health status or location at a facility, and the VIP has authorized disclosure as public information, one may use OrgPI (organizational public information policy - Organizational policy on collection, access, use, or disclosure of public information as defined by the organization or governing jurisdiction) to value ARV-3 indicating that the policy permits the disclosure of VIP sensitive information as coded in ARV-4.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[42].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>To specify the scope of an<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“EMRGONLY”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent directive within a policy domain, use one or more of the following Purpose of Use codes in the ActReason code system OID: 2.16.840.1.113883.5.8.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>ETREAT (Emergency Treatment)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform one or more operations on information for provision of immediately needed health care for an emergent condition.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>BTG (break the glass)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform policy override operations on information for provision of immediately needed health care for an emergent condition affecting potential harm, death or patient safety by end users who are not provisioned for this purpose of use. Includes override of organizational provisioning policies and may include override of subject of care consent directive restricting access.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>ERTREAT (emergency room treatment)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform one or more operations on information for provision of immediately needed health care for an emergent condition in an emergency room or similar emergent care context by end users provisioned for this purpose, which does not constitute as policy override such as in a &quot;&quot;Break the Glass&quot;&quot; purpose of use.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>THREAT (threat)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform one or more operations on information used to prevent injury or disease to living subjects who may be the target of violence.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>DISASTER (disaster) <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform one or more operations on information used for provision of immediately needed health care to a population of living subjects located in a disaster zone.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map: An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“emergency only”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent directive maps to ISO/TS 17975:2015(E)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>5.13 Exceptional access.&quot;</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">To specify the scope of an<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;EMRGONLY&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent directive within a policy domain, use one or more of the following Purpose of Use codes in the ActReason code system OID: 2.16.840.1.113883.5.8.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>ETREAT (Emergency Treatment)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform one or more operations on information for provision of immediately needed health care for an emergent condition.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>BTG (break the glass)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform policy override operations on information for provision of immediately needed health care for an emergent condition affecting potential harm, death or patient safety by end users who are not provisioned for this purpose of use. Includes override of organizational provisioning policies and may include override of subject of care consent directive restricting access.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>ERTREAT (emergency room treatment)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform one or more operations on information for provision of immediately needed health care for an emergent condition in an emergency room or similar emergent care context by end users provisioned for this purpose, which does not constitute as policy override such as in a &quot;&quot;Break the Glass&quot;&quot; purpose of use.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>THREAT (threat)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform one or more operations on information used to prevent injury or disease to living subjects who may be the target of violence.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>DISASTER (disaster) <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Description:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>To perform one or more operations on information used for provision of immediately needed health care to a population of living subjects located in a disaster zone.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map: An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;emergency only&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent directive maps to ISO/TS 17975:2015(E)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>5.13 Exceptional access.&quot;</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[44].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Useful when a more specific jurisdictional or organizational consent directive policy or form is not specified, available, or known, for example, where an individual wishes to opt-out of access, use, or disclosure of some or all of the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">individual’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>information by multiple registries and repositories.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map: An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“expressed”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>opt-out to collection consent directive maps to ISO/TS 17975:2015(E) definitions for<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>“Express</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>or Expressed: Consent to Collect, Use and Disclose personal health information is expressly given by the subject of<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">care”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>and<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“Express</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>or Expressed (and Informed)<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">Denial”.</span></div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">Useful when a more specific jurisdictional or organizational consent directive policy or form is not specified, available, or known, for example, where an individual wishes to opt-out of access, use, or disclosure of some or all of the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">individual&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>information by multiple registries and repositories.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map: An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;expressed&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>opt-out to collection consent directive maps to ISO/TS 17975:2015(E) definitions for<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>&quot;Express</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>or Expressed: Consent to Collect, Use and Disclose personal health information is expressly given by the subject of<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">care&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>and<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;Express</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>or Expressed (and Informed)<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">Denial&quot;.</span></div></div>

  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Useful when a more specific jurisdictional or organizational consent directive policy or form is not specified, available, or known, for example, where an individual wishes to opt-in to access, use, or disclosure of some or all of the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">individual’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>information by multiple registries and repositories.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map: An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“expressed”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent directive maps to ISO/TS 17975:2015(E) Express or Expressed: Consent to Collect, Use and Disclose personal health information is expressly given by the subject of care and<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“Opt-in”.</span></div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">Useful when a more specific jurisdictional or organizational consent directive policy or form is not specified, available, or known, for example, where an individual wishes to opt-in to access, use, or disclosure of some or all of the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">individual&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>information by multiple registries and repositories.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Map: An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;expressed&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent directive maps to ISO/TS 17975:2015(E) Express or Expressed: Consent to Collect, Use and Disclose personal health information is expressly given by the subject of care and<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;Opt-in&quot;.</span></div></div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[49].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A code representing an<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">individual’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent directive that complies with HIPAA Privacy rule 45 CFR Section 164.508 Uses and disclosures for which an authorization is required https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-508.pdf, which is a US Federal law stipulating the policy elements of a valid authorization under this Section.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“authorization”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>is required by the Privacy Rule for uses and disclosures of protected health information not otherwise allowed by the Rule. Where the Privacy Rule requires patient authorization, voluntary consent is not sufficient to permit a use or disclosure of protected health information unless it also satisfies the requirements of a valid authorization. An authorization is a detailed document that gives covered entities permission to use protected health information for specified purposes, which are generally other than treatment, payment, or health care operations, or to disclose protected health information to a third party specified by the individual.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>An authorization must specify a number of elements, including a description of the protected health information to be used and disclosed, the person authorized to make the use or disclosure, the person to whom the covered entity may make the disclosure, an expiration date, and, in some cases, the purpose for which the information may be used or disclosed. With limited exceptions, covered entities may not condition treatment or coverage on the individual providing an authorization. https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/264/what-is-the-difference-between-consent-and-authorization/index.html<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>A HIPAA Authorization must comply with 45 CFR Section164.508(c) Implementation specifications: Core elements and requirements – <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(1) Core elements. A valid authorization under this Section must contain at least the following elements: (i) A description of the information to be used or disclosed that identifies the information in a specific and meaningful fashion. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(ii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, authorized to make the requested use or disclosure. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(iii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, to whom the covered entity may make the requested use or disclosure. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(iv) A description of each purpose of the requested use or disclosure. The statement<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“at</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>the request of the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">individual”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>is a sufficient description of the purpose when an individual initiates the authorization and does not, or elects not to, provide a statement of the purpose. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(v) An expiration date or an expiration event that relates to the individual or the purpose of the use or disclosure. The statement<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“end</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>of the research<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">study,” “none,”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>or similar language is sufficient if the authorization is for a use or disclosure of protected health information for research, including for the creation and maintenance of a research database or research repository. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(vi) Signature of the individual and date. If the authorization is signed by a personal representative of the individual, a description of such representative&#x27;s authority to act for the individual must also be provided. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(2)Required statements. In addition to the core elements, the authorization must contain statements adequate to place the individual on notice of all of the following: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(i) The individual&#x27;s right to revoke the authorization in writing, and either: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(A) The exceptions to the right to revoke and a description of how the individual may revoke the authorization; or (B) To the extent that the information in paragraph (c)(2)(i)(A) of this section is included in the notice required by Section 164.520, a reference to the covered entity&#x27;s notice.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-508.pdf</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">A code representing an<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">individual&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent directive that complies with HIPAA Privacy rule 45 CFR Section 164.508 Uses and disclosures for which an authorization is required https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-508.pdf, which is a US Federal law stipulating the policy elements of a valid authorization under this Section.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;authorization&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>is required by the Privacy Rule for uses and disclosures of protected health information not otherwise allowed by the Rule. Where the Privacy Rule requires patient authorization, voluntary consent is not sufficient to permit a use or disclosure of protected health information unless it also satisfies the requirements of a valid authorization. An authorization is a detailed document that gives covered entities permission to use protected health information for specified purposes, which are generally other than treatment, payment, or health care operations, or to disclose protected health information to a third party specified by the individual.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>An authorization must specify a number of elements, including a description of the protected health information to be used and disclosed, the person authorized to make the use or disclosure, the person to whom the covered entity may make the disclosure, an expiration date, and, in some cases, the purpose for which the information may be used or disclosed. With limited exceptions, covered entities may not condition treatment or coverage on the individual providing an authorization. https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/264/what-is-the-difference-between-consent-and-authorization/index.html<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>A HIPAA Authorization must comply with 45 CFR Section164.508(c) Implementation specifications: Core elements and requirements – <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(1) Core elements. A valid authorization under this Section must contain at least the following elements: (i) A description of the information to be used or disclosed that identifies the information in a specific and meaningful fashion. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(ii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, authorized to make the requested use or disclosure. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(iii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, to whom the covered entity may make the requested use or disclosure. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(iv) A description of each purpose of the requested use or disclosure. The statement<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;at</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>the request of the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">individual&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>is a sufficient description of the purpose when an individual initiates the authorization and does not, or elects not to, provide a statement of the purpose. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(v) An expiration date or an expiration event that relates to the individual or the purpose of the use or disclosure. The statement<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;end</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>of the research<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">study,&quot; &quot;none,&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>or similar language is sufficient if the authorization is for a use or disclosure of protected health information for research, including for the creation and maintenance of a research database or research repository. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(vi) Signature of the individual and date. If the authorization is signed by a personal representative of the individual, a description of such representative&#x27;s authority to act for the individual must also be provided. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(2)Required statements. In addition to the core elements, the authorization must contain statements adequate to place the individual on notice of all of the following: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(i) The individual&#x27;s right to revoke the authorization in writing, and either: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(A) The exceptions to the right to revoke and a description of how the individual may revoke the authorization; or (B) To the extent that the information in paragraph (c)(2)(i)(A) of this section is included in the notice required by Section 164.520, a reference to the covered entity&#x27;s notice.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-508.pdf</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">

  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Used to indicate the legal authority for assigning security labels to HIPAA governed information. In this case, where collection, access, use, or disclosure of healthcare information is governed by a an<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">individual’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>HIPAA Authorization for Disclosure, use<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“HIPAAAuthCD”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>as the security label policy code.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br> Information governed under a HIPAA Authorization for Disclosure has the level of confidentiality protection afforded under the 45 CFR Section 164.506 - Uses and disclosures to carry out treatment, payment, or health care operations https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-506.pdf, which is considered the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“norm”,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>assign the HL7 Confidentiality code<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“N”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>(normal).</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[51].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule 45 CFR Section 164.524 Access of individuals to protected health information https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-524.pdf, stipulating the policy elements of an<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">individual’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>written and signed right of access directive requesting that a covered entity send the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">individual’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>protected health information (PHI) to a third party. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>See 45 CFR 164.524(c)(3)(ii) If an individual&#x27;s request for access directs the covered entity to transmit the copy of protected health information directly to another person designated by the individual, the covered entity must provide the copy to the person designated by the individual. The individual&#x27;s request must be in writing, signed by the individual, and clearly identify the designated person and where to send the copy of protected health information.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-524.pdf <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>This right applies to PHI in a designated record set, which is defined as<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“Designated</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>record set means: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(1) A group of records maintained by or for a covered entity that is: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(i) The medical records and billing records about individuals maintained by or for a covered health care provider; <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(ii) The enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management record systems maintained by or for a health plan; or <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(iii) Used, in whole or in part, by or for the covered entity to make decisions about individuals. [https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.501].<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Also see HHS<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">Individuals’</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information 45 CFR Section 164.524 [https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/access/index.html#maximumflatfee].</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule 45 CFR Section 164.524 Access of individuals to protected health information https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-524.pdf, stipulating the policy elements of an<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">individual&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>written and signed right of access directive requesting that a covered entity send the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">individual&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>protected health information (PHI) to a third party. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>See 45 CFR 164.524(c)(3)(ii) If an individual&#x27;s request for access directs the covered entity to transmit the copy of protected health information directly to another person designated by the individual, the covered entity must provide the copy to the person designated by the individual. [https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.501].<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Also see HHS<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">Individuals&#x27;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information 45 CFR Section 164.524 [https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/access/index.html#maximumflatfee].</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">

  <code>codedContent[53].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>The Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) has developed the Informed Consent and Authorization Toolkit for Minimal Risk Research to facilitate the process of obtaining informed consent and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) authorization from potential research subjects. This toolkit contains information for people responsible for ensuring that potential research subjects are informed in a manner that is consistent with medical ethics and regulatory guidelines. From https://www.ahrq.gov/sites/default/files/publications/files/ictoolkit.pdf.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Used to indicate the legal authority for assigning security labels to governed information. In this case, where collection, access, use, or disclosure of healthcare information is governed by an<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">individual’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>right of access directive under 45 CFR Section 164.508 use<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“CompoundResearchCD”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>as the security label policy code.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Information or biospecimen disclosed under the Common Rule are not protected by the HIPAA Privacy Rule. If protected under other laws such as confidentiality provisions under the Common Rule, assign the HL7 Confidentiality code<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“M”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>(moderate). <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>See ActCode._ActPolicyType._ActPrivacyPolicy._ActPrivacyLaw._ActUSPrivacyLaw.HIPAAAuth (HIPAA Authorization for Disclosure).
