<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[55].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A consent directive compliant with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) definition: Consent of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">subject’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">subject’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Any part of such a declaration which constitutes an infringement of this Regulation shall not be binding.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time. The withdrawal of consent shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal.<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span></span>Prior to giving consent, the data subject shall be informed thereof. It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>When assessing whether consent is freely given, utmost account shall be taken of whether, inter alia, the performance of a contract, including the provision of a service, is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Consent should be given by a clear affirmative act establishing a freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">subject’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her, such as by a written statement, including by electronic means, or an oral statement. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>This could include ticking a box when visiting an internet website, choosing technical settings for information society services or another statement or conduct which clearly indicates in this context the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">subject’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>acceptance of the proposed processing of his or her personal data. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Silence, pre-ticked boxes or inactivity should not therefore constitute consent. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Consent should cover all processing activities carried out for the same purpose or purposes. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>When the processing has multiple purposes, consent should be given for all of them. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">subject’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent is to be given following a request by electronic means, the request must be clear, concise and not unnecessarily disruptive to the use of the service for which it is provided.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">A consent directive compliant with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) definition: Consent of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">subject&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">subject&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language.<span class="diff-in"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span></span>Any part of such a declaration which constitutes an infringement of this Regulation shall not be binding.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Recital 43 Freely given consent* https://gdpr-info.eu/recitals/no-43<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>GDPR Consent Brief https://gdpr-info.eu/issues/consent/ <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Art. 4 GDPR Definitions Art. 6 GDPR Lawfulness of processing Art. 7 GDPR Conditions for consent Art. 8 GDPR Conditions applicable to child&#x27;s consent in relation to information society services Art. 9 GDPR Processing of special categories of personal data Art. 22 GDPR Automated individual decision-making, including profiling Art. 49 GDPR Derogations for specific situations <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Relevant GDPR Recitals:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(32) Conditions for consent (33) Consent to certain areas of scientific research (38) Special protection of children&#x27;s personal data (40) Lawfulness of data processing (42) Burden of proof and requirements for consent (43) Freely given consent (50) Further processing of personal data (51) Protecting sensitive personal data (54) Processing of sensitive data in public health sector (71) Profiling (111) Exceptions for certain cases of international transfers (155) Processing in the employment context (161) Consenting to the participation in clinical trials (171) Repeal of Directive 95/46/EC and transitional provisions</div>

<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Recital 43 Freely given consent* https://gdpr-info.eu/recitals/no-43<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>GDPR Consent Brief https://gdpr-info.eu/issues/consent/ <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Art. 4 GDPR Definitions Art. 6 GDPR Lawfulness of processing Art. 7 GDPR Conditions for consent Art. 8 GDPR Conditions applicable to child&#x27;s consent in relation to information society services Art. 9 GDPR Processing of special categories of personal data Art. 22 GDPR Automated individual decision-making, including profiling Art. 49 GDPR Derogations for specific situations <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Relevant GDPR Recitals:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(32) Conditions for consent (33) Consent to certain areas of scientific research (38) Special protection of children&#x27;s personal data (40) Lawfulness of data processing (42) Burden of proof and requirements for consent (43) Freely given consent (50) Further processing of personal data (51) Protecting sensitive personal data (54) Processing of sensitive data in public health sector (71) Profiling (111) Exceptions for certain cases of international transfers (155) Processing in the employment context (161) Consenting to the participation in clinical trials (171) Repeal of Directive 95/46/EC and transitional provisions</div></div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[56].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A consent directive that complies with regulatory requirements for a consent directive compliant with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) definition: Consent of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">subject’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>GDPR research consent directive has the additional caveat that it is often not possible to fully identify the purpose of personal data processing for scientific research purposes at the time of data collection. Therefore, data subjects should be allowed to give their consent to certain areas of scientific research when in keeping with recognized ethical standards for scientific research. Data subjects should have the opportunity to give their consent only to certain areas of research or parts of research projects to the extent allowed by the intended purpose.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">A consent directive that complies with regulatory requirements for a consent directive compliant with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) definition: Consent of the data subject means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of the data<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">subject&#x27;s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>wishes by which he or she, by a statement or by a clear affirmative action, signifies agreement to the processing of personal data relating to him or her.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>GDPR research consent directive has the additional caveat that it is often not possible to fully identify the purpose of personal data processing for scientific research purposes at the time of data collection. Therefore, data subjects should be allowed to give their consent to certain areas of scientific research when in keeping with recognized ethical standards for scientific research. Data subjects should have the opportunity to give their consent only to certain areas of research or parts of research projects to the extent allowed by the intended purpose.</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[58].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A code representing U.S. Federal laws governing research-related privacy policies known as the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“Common</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">Rule”.</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>The Common Rule is the U.S. Federal regulations governing the protection of human subjects in research (codified at Subpart A of 45 CFR part 46), which has been adopted by 15 U.S. Federal departments and agencies in an effort to promote uniformity, understanding, and compliance with human subject protections. Existing regulations governing the protection of human subjects in Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-regulated research (21 CFR parts 50, 56, 312, and 812) are separate from the Common Rule but include similar requirements.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">A code representing U.S. Federal laws governing research-related privacy policies known as the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;Common</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">Rule&quot;.</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>The Common Rule is the U.S. Federal regulations governing the protection of human subjects in research (codified at Subpart A of 45 CFR part 46), which has been adopted by 15 U.S. Federal departments and agencies in an effort to promote uniformity, understanding, and compliance with human subject protections. Existing regulations governing the protection of human subjects in Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-regulated research (21 CFR parts 50, 56, 312, and 812) are separate from the Common Rule but include similar requirements.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">

HRESCH for applicable security label purpose of use codes.&quot;</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[62].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A code representing Title 38 Section 7332, which is a US Federal law stipulating the privacy rights of veterans diagnosed and treated for substance use disorders, infection with the human immunodeficiency virus, or sickle cell anemia.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Title 38 Section 7332 - Confidentiality of certain medical records<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/granule/USCODE-2011-title38/USCODE-2011-title38-partV-chap73-subchapIII-sec7332/content-detail.html<span class="diff-out"><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br></span>(1) Records of the identity, diagnosis, prognosis, or treatment of any patient or subject which are maintained in connection with the performance of any program or activity (including education, training, treatment, rehabilitation, or research) relating to drug abuse, alcoholism or alcohol abuse, infection with the human immunodeficiency virus, or sickle cell anemia which is carried out by or for the Department under this title shall, except as provided in subsections (e) and (f), be confidential, and (section 5701 of this title to the contrary notwithstanding) such records may be disclosed only for the purposes and under the circumstances expressly authorized under subsection (b).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(2) Paragraph (1) prohibits the disclosure to any person or entity other than the patient or subject concerned of the fact that a special given record referred to in subsection (a) is maintained, gives written consent, the content of such record may be disclosed by the Secretary as follows: <span class="ws" title="line authority charged under Federal or State law with the protection of the public health, and to which Federal or State law requires disclosure of such record, if a qualified representative of such authority has made a written request that such record be provided as required pursuant to such law for a purpose authorized by such law.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(ii) A break">&#182;</span><br>(D) If authorized by an appropriate order of a court of competent jurisdiction granted after application showing good cause therefor. In assessing good cause the court shall weigh the public interest and the need for disclosure against the injury to the patient or subject, to the physician-patient relationship, and to the treatment services. Upon the granting of such order, the court, in determining the extent to which any disclosure of all or any part of any record is necessary, shall impose appropriate safeguards against unauthorized disclosure.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(E) To an entity described in paragraph (1)(B) of section 5701(k) of this title, but only to the extent authorized by such section.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>(F) (i) To a representative of a patient who lacks decision-making capacity, when a practitioner deems the content of the given record necessary for that   <code>codedContent[62].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Used to indicate the legal authority for assigning security labels to governed information. In this case, where collection, access, use, or disclosure of healthcare information is governed by 38 U.S. Code Section 7332 - Confidentiality of certain medical records<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/granule/USCODE-2011-title38/USCODE-2011-title38-partV-chap73-subchapIII-sec7332/content-detail.html use<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“Title38Section7332”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>as the security label policy code. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Since information governed by a Title 38 Section 7332 has a level of confidentiality protection that is more stringent than the normal level of protection under HIPAA 45 CFR Section 164.506 Uses and disclosures to carry out treatment, payment, or health care operations https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-506.pdf, assign the HL7 Confidentiality code<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“R”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>(restricted).</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">Used to indicate the legal authority for assigning security labels to governed information. <div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[64].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule (45 CFR Section 164.508) Uses and disclosures for which an authorization is required https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-508.pdf, which stipulates the process by which a covered entity seeks agreement from an individual to use or disclose protected health information for other purposes, or to authorize another covered entity to disclose protected health information to the requesting covered entity, are termed &quot;&quot;authorizations&quot;&quot;.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“authorization”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>is required by the Privacy Rule for uses and disclosures of protected health information not otherwise allowed by the Rule. Where the Privacy Rule requires patient authorization, voluntary consent is not sufficient to permit a use or disclosure of protected health information unless it also satisfies the requirements of a valid authorization. An authorization is a detailed document that gives covered entities permission to use protected health information for specified purposes, which are generally other than treatment, payment, or health care operations, or to disclose protected health information to a third party specified by the individual.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>An authorization must specify a number of elements, including a description of the protected health information to be used and disclosed, the person authorized to make the use or disclosure, the person to whom the covered entity may make the disclosure, an expiration date, and, in some cases, the purpose for which the information may be used or disclosed. With limited exceptions, covered entities may not condition treatment or coverage on the individual providing an authorization. https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/264/what-is-the-difference-between-consent-and-authorization/index.html</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule (45 CFR Section 164.508) Uses and disclosures for which an authorization is required https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-508.pdf, which stipulates the process by which a covered entity seeks agreement from an individual to use or disclose protected health information for other purposes, or to authorize another covered entity to disclose protected health information to the requesting covered entity, are termed &quot;&quot;authorizations&quot;&quot;.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>An<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">&quot;authorization&quot;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>is required by the Privacy Rule for uses and disclosures of protected health information not otherwise allowed by the Rule. Where the Privacy Rule requires patient authorization, voluntary consent is not sufficient to permit a use or disclosure of protected health information unless it also satisfies the requirements of a valid authorization. An authorization is a detailed document that gives covered entities permission to use protected health information for specified purposes, which are generally other than treatment, payment, or health care operations, or to disclose protected health information to a third party specified by the individual.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>An authorization must specify a number of elements, including a description of the protected health information to be used and disclosed, the person authorized to make the use or disclosure, the person to whom the covered entity may make the disclosure, an expiration date, and, in some cases, the purpose for which the information may be used or disclosed. With limited exceptions, covered entities may not condition treatment or coverage on the individual providing an authorization. https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/264/what-is-the-difference-between-consent-and-authorization/index.html</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[65].definition</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule 45 CFR Section 164.524 Access of individuals to protected health information https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-524, which stipulates that an individual has a right of access to inspect and obtain a copy of protected health information about the individual in a designated record set, for as long as the protected health information is maintained in the designated record set with exceptions stipulated in HIPAA Privacy Rule Section 164.524. Exceptions include psychotherapy notes and information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal, or administrative action or proceeding.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If an individual&#x27;s request for access directs the covered entity to transmit the copy of protected health information directly to another person designated by the individual, the covered entity must provide the copy to the person designated by the individual. The individual&#x27;s request must be in writing, signed by the individual, and clearly identify the designated person and where to send the copy of protected health information.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>For discussion on extent of right, grounds for denial, and documentation requirements see: HHS<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">Individuals’</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information 45 CFR Section 164.524 https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/access/index.html and HHS FAQ on Right of Access vs. HIPAA Authorization https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/2041/why-depend-on-the-individuals-right/index.html</div>
  <div class="ri-who">LLM: <div class="cell">A code representing U.S. Public Law 104-191 Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule 45 CFR Section 164.524 Access of individuals to protected health information https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-524, which stipulates that an individual has a right of access to inspect and obtain a copy of protected health information about the individual in a designated record set, for as long as the protected health information is maintained in the designated record set with exceptions stipulated in HIPAA Privacy Rule Section 164.524. Exceptions include psychotherapy notes and information compiled in reasonable anticipation of, or for use in, a civil, criminal, or administrative action or proceeding.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>If an individual&#x27;s request for access directs the covered entity to transmit the copy of protected health information directly to another person designated by the individual, the covered entity must provide the copy to the person designated by the individual. The individual&#x27;s request must be in writing, signed by the individual, and clearly identify the designated person and where to send the copy of protected health information.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>For discussion on extent of right, grounds for denial, and documentation requirements see: HHS<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-in">Individuals&#x27;</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>Right under HIPAA to Access their Health Information 45 CFR Section 164.524 https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/access/index.html and HHS FAQ on Right of Access vs. HIPAA Authorization https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/2041/why-depend-on-the-individuals-right/index.html</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">

  <code>codedContent[65].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>Used to indicate the legal authority for assigning security labels to governed information. In this case, where collection, access, use, or disclosure of healthcare information is governed under 45 CFR Section 164.5224 use<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“HIPAAROA”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>as the security label policy code.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Information disclosed under a HIPAA 42 CFR Section 164.524 no longer has the level of confidentiality protection afforded under the 45 CFR Section 164.506 - Uses and disclosures to carry out treatment, payment, or health care operations https://www.gpo.gov/fdsys/pkg/CFR-2017-title45-vol1/pdf/CFR-2017-title45-vol1-sec164-508.pdf, which is considered the<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“norm”,</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>assign the HL7 Confidentiality code<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">“M”</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>(moderate), which may be protected under other laws such as the Federal Trade Commission privacy and security regulations.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0717</div>
  <code>codedContent[68].comment</code>
  <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>This processing policy code offers an escape-hatch to countries like Denmark and Austria: they simply declare their national healthcare data exchanges to be necessary for the management of their healthcare system. This allows them to establish an opt-out mechanism under the GDPR, whereas normally GDPR would be opt-in when it comes to such national exchanges.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The description is based on the following GDPR provisions:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Article 9.1, and 9.2.c and 9.2.h, 9.3 https://gdpr-info.eu/art-9-gdpr/<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>1. Processing of personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, or trade union membership, and the processing of genetic data, biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health or data concerning a natural<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span><span class="diff-out">person’s</span><span class="ws" title="leading space">&middot;</span>sex life or sexual orientation shall be prohibited.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>2. Paragraph 1 shall not apply if one of the following applies: (c) processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person where the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent; (h) processing is necessary for the purposes of preventive or occupational medicine, for the assessment of the working capacity of the employee, medical diagnosis, the provision of health or social care or treatment or the management of health or social care systems and services on the basis of Union or Member State law or pursuant to contract with a health professional and subject to the conditions and safeguards referred to in paragraph 3;<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>3. Personal data referred to in paragraph 1 may be processed for the purposes referred to in point (h) of paragraph 2 when those data are processed by or under the responsibility of a professional subject to the obligation of professional secrecy under Union or Member State law or rules established by national competent bodies or by another person also subject to an obligation of secrecy under Union or Member State law or rules established by national competent bodies.</div>

This code system includes 2010 U.S. Census Bureau occupation codes with modifications made by CDC for unpaid workers and military occupations. The 2010 Census occupation categories are based on the 2010 BLS Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) system. The PH_Industry_CDC_Census2010 code system should be used in conjunction with this occupation code system when coding both industry and occupation.   <div class="cell"><p class="diff-note">Only the highlighted words differ.</p>The HGNC gene table carries the GENE ID, gene symbol and full gene name. The GENE ID is specific to the species. #### Published document &mdash; Non-ASCII characters in the emitted corpus <span class="ri-count">&mdash; 14 items</span>

<div class="ri-blurb">Every character above ASCII that survives into the extracted corpus, counted, and checked against every character <code>hl7.terminology.r5</code> publishes. Characters already repaired by ADR-0008 D7 &mdash; the double-encoded non-breaking space in table 0301 and the Symbol-font bullets in 0964 &mdash; no longer appear here, which is the check that the repair worked. <b>Every one of them also appears in THO</b>, so none is a problem: whatever this corpus carries, the terminology it will sit beside already publishes the same character. For the two that once looked doubtful &mdash; NCPDP's slashed zero and the non-breaking hyphen &mdash; THO carries not just the character but the identical text.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0078</div>
  <div class="cell">HL7-defined code system of concepts which specify a categorical assessment of an observation value.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the OBX segment.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Notes: This is being communicated in v2.x in OBX-8, in v3 in ObservationInterpretation (CWE) in R1 (Representative Realm) and in FHIR Observation.interpretation.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0389</div>
  <div class="cell">HL7-defined code system of concepts identifying the repeat status for the analyte/result (e.g. original, rerun, repeat, reflex).<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The following are assumptions regarding the table values:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Repeated without dilution — performed usually to confirm correctness of results (e.g., in case of results flagged as &quot;Panic&quot; or mechanical failures).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Repeated with dilution — performed usually in the case the original result exceeded the measurement range (technical limits).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Reflex test — this test is performed as the consequence of rules triggered based on other test result(s).<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the Test Code Detail (TCD) segment.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">HL7-defined code system of concepts identifying the repeat status for the analyte/result (e.g. original, rerun, repeat, reflex).<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The following are assumptions regarding the table values:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Repeated without dilution — performed usually to confirm correctness of results (e.g., in case of results flagged as &quot;Panic&quot; or mechanical failures).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Repeated with dilution — performed usually in the case the original result exceeded the measurement range (technical limits).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Reflex test — this test is performed as the consequence of rules triggered based on other test result(s).<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the Test Code Detail (TCD) segment.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0467</div>
  <div class="cell">The OPPS functionality of the Integrated Outpatient Code Editor (I/OCE) software was developed for the implementation of the Medicare outpatient prospective payment system mandated by the 1997 Balanced Budget Act. CMS released the proposed OPPS rules using the Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) system in the September 8, 1998 Federal Register. Final regulations were published in the April 7, 2000 Federal Register and the system became effective for Medicare on August 1, 2000.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the GP1 segment.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The APC-based OPPS developed by CMS is the outpatient equivalent of the inpatient, DRG-based PPS. The APC system establishes groups of covered services so that the services within each group are comparable clinically and with respect to the use of resources.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Hospitals are required to use HCPCS when billing for outpatient services.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The OCE not only identifies individual errors but also indicates what actions should be taken and the reasons why these actions are necessary. In order to accommodate this functionality, the OCE is structured to return lists of edit numbers. This structure facilitates the linkage between the actions being taken, the reasons for the actions and the information on the claim (e.g., a specific diagnosis) that caused the action. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>In general, the OCE performs all functions that require specific reference to HCPCS codes, HCPCS modifiers and ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes (ICD-9-CM diagnosis codes for historical claims with From Dates prior to 10/1/2015). Since these coding systems are complex and annually updated, the centralization of the direct reference to these codes and modifiers in a single program reduces effort and reduces the chance of inconsistent processing.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>This is a CMS maintained list of edits: Please see the following for additional information: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/index.html<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/Background.htmlC<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/OCEQtrReleaseSpecs.html</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">The OPPS functionality of the Integrated Outpatient Code Editor (I/OCE) software was developed for the implementation of the Medicare outpatient prospective payment system mandated by the 1997 Balanced Budget Act. Since these coding systems are complex and annually updated, the centralization of the direct reference to these codes and modifiers in a single program reduces effort and reduces the chance of inconsistent processing.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>This is a CMS maintained list of edits: Please see the following for additional information: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/index.html<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/Background.htmlC<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>•<span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>https://www.cms.gov/Medicare/Coding/OutpatientCodeEdit/OCEQtrReleaseSpecs.html</div></div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0719</div>
  <div class="cell">A code specifying the particular kind of Act that the Act-instance represents within its class.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Constraints: The kind of Act (e.g. physical examination, serum potassium, inpatient encounter, charge financial transaction, etc.) is specified with a code from one of several, typically external, coding systems. The coding system will depend on the class of Act, such as LOINC for observations, etc.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Conceptually, the Act.code must be a specialization of the Act.classCode. This is why the structure of ActClass domain should be reflected in the superstructure of the ActCode domain and then individual codes or externally referenced vocabularies subordinated under these domains that reflect the ActClass structure.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Act.classCode and Act.code are not modifiers of each other but the Act.code concept should really imply the Act.classCode concept. For a negative example, it is not appropriate to use an Act.code &quot;potassium&quot; together with and Act.classCode for &quot;laboratory observation&quot; to somehow mean &quot;potassium laboratory observation&quot; and then use the same Act.code for &quot;potassium&quot; together with Act.classCode for &quot;medication&quot; to mean &quot;substitution of potassium&quot;. This mutually modifying use of Act.code and Act.classCode is not permitted.Code system of concepts specifying the reason for the restricted access.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the ARV segment.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">A code specifying the particular kind of Act that the Act-instance represents within its class.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Constraints: The kind of Act (e.g. physical examination, serum potassium, inpatient encounter, charge financial transaction, etc.) is specified with a code from one of several, typically external, coding systems. The coding system will depend on the class of Act, such as LOINC for observations, etc.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Conceptually, the Act.code must be a specialization of the Act.classCode. This is why the structure of ActClass domain should be reflected in the superstructure of the ActCode domain and then individual codes or externally referenced vocabularies subordinated under these domains that reflect the ActClass structure.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Act.classCode and Act.code are not modifiers of each other but the Act.code concept should really imply the Act.classCode concept. For a negative example, it is not appropriate to use an Act.code &quot;potassium&quot; together with and Act.classCode for &quot;laboratory observation&quot; to somehow mean &quot;potassium laboratory observation&quot; and then use the same Act.code for &quot;potassium&quot; together with Act.classCode for &quot;medication&quot; to mean &quot;substitution of potassium&quot;. This mutually modifying use of Act.code and Act.classCode is not permitted.Code system of concepts specifying the reason for the restricted access.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the ARV segment.</div></div>
</div>

  <div class="cell">National Uniform Billing Committee (NUBC) UB-04 Data Specifications Manual, UB form locator 67, Present on Admission (POA) Indicator. Code identifying a diagnosis that<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>was present at the time the order for inpatient admission occurs. POA indicator is assigned to all diagnoses as defined in Appendix I of the &quot;ICD-9-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting&quot; or &quot;ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting (appropriate to the ICD revision used).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br> <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The UB-04 Data Specifications Manual with the codes is available by subscription from NUBC at http://www.nubc.org/become.html.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Used in HL7 Version 2.x messaging in the DG1 segment.</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0203</div>
  <div class="cell">Use case: This is a registration number that identifies an individual or organization relative to controlled substance regulation and transactions. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>A DEA number has a very precise and widely accepted meaning within the United States. Surprisingly, the US Drug Enforcement Administration does not solely assign DEA numbers in the United States. Hospitals have the authority to issue DEA numbers to their medical residents. These DEA numbers are based upon the hospital’s DEA number, but the authority rests with the hospital on the assignment to the residents. Thus, DEA as an Identifier Type is necessary in addition to DEA as an Assigning Authority.</div>

  <div class="cell">Also referred to as HPID (Health Plan Identifier).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note: The code value ‘XV’ is used in CMS mandated Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) transactions.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">Also referred to as HPID (Health Plan Identifier).<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note: The code value ‘XV’ is used in CMS mandated Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) transactions.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0211</div>
  <div class="cell">Note that the code contains a space, i.e., “ISO IR87”.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The JIS X 0208 needs an escape sequence. In Japan, the escape technique is ISO 2022. From basic ASCII, escape sequence “escape” $ B (in HEX, 1B 24 42) lets the parser know that following bytes should be handled 2-byte wise. Back to ASCII is 1B 28 42.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">Note that the code contains a space, i.e., “ISO IR87”.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The JIS X 0208 needs an escape sequence. In Japan, the escape technique is ISO 2022. From basic ASCII, escape sequence “escape” $ B (in HEX, 1B 24 42) lets the parser know that following bytes should be handled 2-byte wise. Back to ASCII is 1B 28 42.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0211</div>
  <div class="cell">Does not need an escape sequence.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>BIG-5 does not need an escape sequence. ASCII is a 7 bit character set, which means that the top bit of the byte is “0”. The parser knows that when the top bit of the byte is “0”, the character set is ASCII. When it is “1”, the following bytes should be handled as 2 bytes (or more). No escape technique is needed. However, since some servers do not correctly interpret when they receive a top bit “1”, it is advised, in internet RFC, to not use these kind of non-safe non-escape extension.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">Does not need an escape sequence.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>BIG-5 does not need an escape sequence. ASCII is a 7 bit character set, which means that the top bit of the byte is “0”. The parser knows that when the top bit of the byte is “0”, the character set is ASCII. When it is “1”, the following bytes should be handled as 2 bytes (or more). No escape technique is needed. However, since some servers do not correctly interpret when they receive a top bit “1”, it is advised, in internet RFC, to not use these kind of non-safe non-escape extension.</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0211</div>
  <div class="cell">UTF-8 is a variable-length encoding, each code value is represented by 1,2 or 3 bytes, depending on the code value. 7 bit ASCII is a proper subset of UTF-8. Note that the code contains a space before UTF but not before and after the hyphen. Since UTF-8 represents the full UNICODE character set, the following restriction apply to its use: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>1. UTF-8 must be the default encoding of the message, UTF-8 cannot be specified as an additional character set in MSH-18<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>2. There are no other character sets allowed in a message where UTF-8 is the default encoding in the message.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>In other words, UNICODE UTF-8 can only be specified as a single value in MSH-18<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>3. A message encoded in UTF-8 must not use a Byte Order Mark (BOM).</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">UTF-8 is a variable-length encoding, each code value is represented by 1,2 or 3 bytes, depending on the code value. 7 bit ASCII is a proper subset of UTF-8. Note that the code contains a space before UTF but not before and after the hyphen. Since UTF-8 represents the full UNICODE character set, the following restriction apply to its use: <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>1. UTF-8 must be the default encoding of the message, UTF-8 cannot be specified as an additional character set in MSH-18<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>2. There are no other character sets allowed in a message where UTF-8 is the default encoding in the message.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>In other words, UNICODE UTF-8 can only be specified as a single value in MSH-18<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>3. A message encoded in UTF-8 must not use a Byte Order Mark (BOM).</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0340</div>
  <div class="cell">Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) including modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note: The HCPCS code is divided into three &quot;levels.&quot;<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Level I includes the entire CPT-4 code by reference.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Level II includes the American Dental Association’s Current Dental Terminology (CDT-2) code by reference.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Level II also includes the genuine HCPCS codes, approved and maintained jointly by the Alpha-Numeric Editorial Panel, consisting of CMS, the Health Insurance Association of America, and the Blue Cross and Blue Shield Association. Level III are codes developed locally by Medicare carriers.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The HCPCS modifiers are divided into the same three levels, I being CPT-4 modifiers, II CDT-2 and genuine HCPCS modifiers, and III being locally agreed modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The genuine HCPCS codes and modifiers of level II can be found at http://www.hcfa.gov/stats/anhcpcdl.htm. CMS distributes the HCPCS codes via the National Technical Information Service (NTIS, www.ntis.gov) and NTIS distribution includes the CDT-2 part of HCPCS Level II, but does not include the CPT-4 part (Level I). CMS may distribute the CPT-4 part to ist contractors.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) including modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Usage Note: The HCPCS code is divided into three &quot;levels.&quot;<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Level I includes the entire CPT-4 code by reference.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Level II includes the American Dental Association’s Current Dental Terminology (CDT-2) code by reference.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Level II also includes the genuine HCPCS codes, approved and maintained jointly by the Alpha-Numeric Editorial Panel, consisting of CMS, the Health Insurance Association of America, and the Blue Cross and Blue Shield Association. Level III are codes developed locally by Medicare carriers.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The HCPCS modifiers are divided into the same three levels, I being CPT-4 modifiers, II CDT-2 and genuine HCPCS modifiers, and III being locally agreed modifiers.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The genuine HCPCS codes and modifiers of level II can be found at http://www.hcfa.gov/stats/anhcpcdl.htm. CMS distributes the HCPCS codes via the National Technical Information Service (NTIS, www.ntis.gov) and NTIS distribution includes the CDT-2 part of HCPCS Level II, but does not include the CPT-4 part (Level I). CMS may distribute the CPT-4 part to ist contractors.</div></div>
</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0396</div>
  <div class="cell">The HGNC gene table carries the GENE ID, gene symbol and full gene name. The GENE ID is specific to the species. The gene symbol and name will be shared by all species with the same gene. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The HGNC-Symb table carries only human genes. The code for this coding system is the HGNC gene code, the &quot;name&quot; or print string is the HGNC gene symbol. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>More than 28,000 human gene symbols and names have been assigned so far, but some human genes lack an HGNC code and symbol. These are mostly non protein coding genes.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br></div>

The gene symbol and name will be shared by all species with the same gene. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The HGNC-Symb table carries only human genes. The code for this coding system is the HGNC gene code, the &quot;name&quot; or print string is the HGNC gene symbol. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>More than 28,000 human gene symbols and names have been assigned so far, but some human genes lack an HGNC code and symbol. These are mostly non protein coding genes.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br></div></div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0396</div>
  <div class="cell">Percy C, VanHolten V, and Muir C, editors. International Classification of Diseases for Oncology. Second Edition. Geneva: World Health Organization; 1990.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The ICD-9 neoplasm structure did not include morphology and there was a growing interest by physicians to establish a coding system for morphology.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>ICD-O is used in cancer registries (and other related areas) for coding the topography (site) and morphology of a neoplasm. The topography code uses similar categories as ICD-10 for malignant neoplasms allowing greater specificity for the site of non-malignant neoplasms than in ICD-10.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The topography code consists of an alphabetic character (the letter C) followed by two numeric digits, a decimal point, and a numeric digit. The morphology code consists of a 6-digit numeric code which consists of three parts: histologic type (4-digit), behavior code (1-digit), and grading or differentiation (1-digit). ICD-O-2 is used for tumors diagnosed prior to 2001.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">Percy C, VanHolten V, and Muir C, editors. International Classification of Diseases for Oncology. Second Edition. Geneva: World Health Organization; 1990.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The ICD-9 neoplasm structure did not include morphology and there was a growing interest by physicians to establish a coding system for morphology.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>ICD-O is used in cancer registries (and other related areas) for coding the topography (site) and morphology of a neoplasm. The topography code uses similar categories as ICD-10 for malignant neoplasms allowing greater specificity for the site of non-malignant neoplasms than in ICD-10.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The topography code consists of an alphabetic character (the letter C) followed by two numeric digits, a decimal point, and a numeric digit. The morphology code consists of a 6-digit numeric code which consists of three parts: histologic type (4-digit), behavior code (1-digit), and grading or differentiation (1-digit). ICD-O-2 is used for tumors diagnosed prior to 2001.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0396</div>
  <div class="cell">Fritz A, Percy C, Jack A, Shanmugaratnam K, Sobin L, Parkin D, et al, editors. International Classification of Diseases for Oncology. Third Edition. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2000.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The ICD-9 neoplasm structure did not include morphology and there was a growing interest by physicians to establish a coding system for morphology.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>ICD-O is used in cancer registries (and other related areas) for coding the topography (site) and morphology of a neoplasm. The topography code uses similar categories as ICD-10 for malignant neoplasms allowing greater specificity for the site of non-malignant neoplasms than in ICD-10.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The topography code consists of an alphabetic character (the letter C) followed by two numeric digits, a decimal point, and a numeric digit. The morphology code consists of a 6-digit numeric code which consists of three parts: histologic type, behavior code, and grading or differentiation. In the third edition the morphology codes were revised, especially for leukemias and lymphomas. ICD-O-3 is used for tumors diagnosed in 2001 and later.</div>

International Classification of Diseases for Oncology. Third Edition. The topography code uses similar categories as ICD-10 for malignant neoplasms allowing greater specificity for the site of non-malignant neoplasms than in ICD-10.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The topography code consists of an alphabetic character (the letter C) followed by two numeric digits, a decimal point, and a numeric digit. The morphology code consists of a 6-digit numeric code which consists of three parts: histologic type, behavior code, and grading or differentiation. <div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0396</div>
  <div class="cell">Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC®) provides a set of universal codes and names for identifying laboratory and other clinical observations. One of the main goals of LOINC is to facilitate the exchange and pooling of results for clinical care, outcomes management, and research. LOINC was initiated by Regenstrief Institute research scientists who continue to develop it with the collaboration of the LOINC Committee. The LOINC table, LOINC codes, and LOINC panels and forms file are copyright © 1995-2011, Regenstrief Institute, Inc. and the LOINC Committee and available at no cost (http://loinc.org) under the license at http://loinc.org/terms-of-use.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The laboratory portion of the LOINC database contains the usual clinical laboratory categories of chemistry, hematology, serology, microbiology (including parasitology and virology), toxicology; as well as categories for drugs and the cell counts, antibiotic susceptibilities, and more. The clinical portion of the LOINC database includes entries for vital signs, hemodynamics, intake/output, EKG, obstetric ultrasound, cardiac echo, radiology report titles, pulmonary ventilator management, document and section titles, patient assessment instruments (e.g. Glascow Coma Score, PHQ-9 depression scale, CMS-required patient assessment instruments), and other clinical observations.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">Logical Observation Identifiers Names and Codes (LOINC®) provides a set of universal codes and names for identifying laboratory and other clinical observations. One of the main goals of LOINC is to facilitate the exchange and pooling of results for clinical care, outcomes management, and research. LOINC was initiated by Regenstrief Institute research scientists who continue to develop it with the collaboration of the LOINC Committee. The LOINC table, LOINC codes, and LOINC panels and forms file are copyright © 1995-2011, Regenstrief Institute, Inc. and the LOINC Committee and available at no cost (http://loinc.org) under the license at http://loinc.org/terms-of-use.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The laboratory portion of the LOINC database contains the usual clinical laboratory categories of chemistry, hematology, serology, microbiology (including parasitology and virology), toxicology; as well as categories for drugs and the cell counts, antibiotic susceptibilities, and more. The clinical portion of the LOINC database includes entries for vital signs, hemodynamics, intake/output, EKG, obstetric ultrasound, cardiac echo, radiology report titles, pulmonary ventilator management, document and section titles, patient assessment instruments (e.g. Glascow Coma Score, PHQ-9 depression scale, CMS-required patient assessment instruments), and other clinical observations.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0396</div>
  <div class="cell">LRG is a manually curated record that contains stable and thus, un-versioned reference sequences designed specifically for reporting sequence variants with clinical implications. <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>It provides a genomic DNA sequence representation of a single gene that is idealized, has a permanent ID (with no versioning), and core content that never changes. Their database includes maps to NCBI, Ensembl and USCS reference sequences.<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span></div>

Their database includes maps to NCBI, Ensembl and USCS reference sequences.<span class="ws" title="trailing space">&middot;</span></div></div>

  <div class="cell">NCPDP maintain code list associated with the specified Data Element (nnnn) and Segment (sss).<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The Segment portion is optional if there is no specialization of the Data Element codes between segments.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Examples:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="3 spaces">&middot;&middot;&middot;</span>NCPDP1131RES = code set defined for NCPDP data element 1131 as used in the RES segment (Code List Qualifier – Response Code)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="3 spaces">&middot;&middot;&middot;</span>NCPDP1131STS = code set defined for NCPDP data element 1131 as used in the STS segment (Code List Qualifier – Reject Code)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="3 spaces">&middot;&middot;&middot;</span>NCPDP9701 = code set defined for NCPDP data element 9701 (Individual Relationship, Coded).<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>No specialization to a segment exists for this data element.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>National Council for Prescription Drug Programs, 924Ø East Raintree Drive, Scottsdale, AZ<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>8526Ø.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Phone: (48Ø) 477-1ØØØ<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>Fax: (48Ø) 767-1Ø42<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>e-mail: ncpdp@ncpdp.org<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>www.ncpdp.org</div>

<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0506</div>
  <div class="cell">Where a set of two or more orders exist and the Nurse, or other caregiver, has the prerogative to choose which order will be administered at a particular point in time.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>For example,<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Milk of Magnesia PO 30 ml qhs (at bedtime)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Dulcolax Supp R @ hs prn<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Colace 100 mg capsule PO bid <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The nurse would be administering MOM, but may add the Colace and may also give the Dulcolax Supp as needed to promote and maintain regularity.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">Where a set of two or more orders exist and the Nurse, or other caregiver, has the prerogative to choose which order will be administered at a particular point in time.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>For example,<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Milk of Magnesia PO 30 ml qhs (at bedtime)<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Dulcolax Supp R @ hs prn<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Colace 100 mg capsule PO bid <span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>The nurse would be administering MOM, but may add the Colace and may also give the Dulcolax Supp as needed to promote and maintain regularity.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0506</div>
  <div class="cell">A tapering order is one in which the same drug is used, but it has a declining dosage over a number of days.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>For example, Decadron 0.5 mg is often ordered this way.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The order would look like this:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Decadron 0.5 mg qid (four times a day) for 2 days, then<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Decadron 0.5 mg tid (three times a day) for 2 days, then<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Decadron 0.5 mg bid (twice a day) for 2 days, then<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Decadron 0.5 mg qd (daily) for 2 days, then stop.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">A tapering order is one in which the same drug is used, but it has a declining dosage over a number of days.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>For example, Decadron 0.5 mg is often ordered this way.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>The order would look like this:<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Decadron 0.5 mg qid (four times a day) for 2 days, then<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Decadron 0.5 mg tid (three times a day) for 2 days, then<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Decadron 0.5 mg bid (twice a day) for 2 days, then<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="tab">&#8677;</span>Decadron 0.5 mg qd (daily) for 2 days, then stop.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0557</div>
  <div class="cell">A legal entity that controls and directs a worker under an express or implied contract of employment and a salary or wages in compensation.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>In worker’s compensation cases, the Employer may be the “organization” responsible for paying the healthcare charges for employment related illness or injury.</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">A legal entity that controls and directs a worker under an express or implied contract of employment and a salary or wages in compensation.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br><span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>In worker’s compensation cases, the Employer may be the “organization” responsible for paying the healthcare charges for employment related illness or injury.</div></div>
</div>
<div class="ri-item ri-informational">
  <div class="ri-key">0617</div>
  <div class="cell">Identifies an address for mail correspondence from a healthcare provider as stipulated by the subject.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>For example, under the tenets of certain privacy regulations, it is exclusive to the patient and is typically maintained at the encounter or visit level versus the person level as it only has relevance to the specifics of a given encounter.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>This is an exception category of address in that the patient has stipulated that they want all correspondence relevant to a given encounter sent to this address in lieu of any other address on file.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Providers are required to accommodate such requests under HIPAA promulgated regulation.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Note that mailing and legal address may be mutually exclusive as defined below.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>(Implementors are reminded that although the privacy regulation requires the provider to honor such requests, it does require the provider to enquire whether the patient has a preferred address other than the one volunteered.)</div>
  <div class="ri-who">As emitted — outstanding site marked: <div class="cell">Identifies an address for mail correspondence from a healthcare provider as stipulated by the subject.<span class="ws" title="line break">&#182;</span><br>For example, under the tenets of certain privacy regulations, it is exclusive to the patient and is typically maintained at the encounter or visit level versus the person level as it only has relevance to the specifics of a given encounter.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>This is an exception category of address in that the patient has stipulated that they want all correspondence relevant to a given encounter sent to this address in lieu of any other address on file.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Providers are required to accommodate such requests under HIPAA promulgated regulation.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>Note that mailing and legal address may be mutually exclusive as defined below.<span class="ws" title="2 spaces">&middot;&middot;</span>(Implementors are reminded that although the privacy regulation requires the provider to honor such requests, it does require the provider to enquire whether the patient has a preferred address other than the one volunteered.)</div></div>
</div>
